item.title: Sabalenka bundled out of China Open by Czech Bartunkova
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka crashed out of the China Open in the third round following a 6-4 6-3 by Czech Nikola Bartunkova in Beijing on Sunday, the latest setback in a frustrating season for the world number two.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Aryna Sabalenka crashed out of the China Open in the third round following a 6-4 6-3 by Czech Nikola Bartunkova in Beijing on Sunday, the latest setback in a frustrating season for the world number two. Sabalenka was broken in the opening game and squandered five opportunities to break back in the sixth game of the first set, before going on to lose the match in an hour and 35 minutes. "I focused on myself, to be calm. Aryna is great. She's a legend. She's a Grand Slam champion," Bartunkova, 20, said. Four-times major winner Sabalenka has not lifted a trophy since completing the "Sunshine Double" with victories in Indian Wells and Miami earlier this year. The Belarusian made it to the US Open final last month but was [USN:L1N45406Y TEXT:"beaten by Elena Rybakina"], ensuring she would finish the season without a Grand Slam win for the first time since 2022. Rybakina replaced Sabalenka at the top of the world rankings after the US Open.

item.title: Padres ponder what might have been on roof-aided out in loss to Brewers
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers manager Pat Murphy credited the team's legendary late broadcaster Bob Uecker for an unlikely boost in the ninth inning to help preserve the 3-2 victory over visiting San Diego in the opener of the NLDS on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers manager Pat Murphy credited the team's legendary late broadcaster Bob Uecker for an unlikely boost in the ninth inning to help preserve the 3-2 victory over visiting San Diego in the opener of the NLDS on Saturday. With one out in the ninth and the Brewers clinging to a one-run lead, San Diego had a runner on first when Ty France hit a drive to left field off closer Trevor Megill that struck a cable on the closed roof of American Family Field. The ball stayed in play and was caught by left fielder Jackson Chourio for the second out. Megill then retired Jackson Merrill on a fly ball to right field to give Milwaukee the victory. "I think the only thing that you could probably figure on the ball that everybody's going to be talking about is that ‘Ueck' decided to put his hand on it and swat it down so Chourio could catch it," Murphy said afterward. "So thanks, Ueck." Uecker, the comedic former ballplayer turned broadcaster who was the radio voice of the Brewers for more than 50 years, died before the 2025 season at age 90. The ground rules for American Family Field say that a batted ball that strikes the roof, roof truss, roof cable or any cabling over fair territory is in play. If caught by a fielder, the batter is out. If the ball strikes any of those same structures over foul territory, it's a dead ball. A third rule says if the ball strikes those structures over fair territory and lands foul, it's a foul ball. The Padres challenged whether the ball was fair or foul, but the on-field call that it was an out was upheld. Padres manager Craig Stammen thought the ball would have been a home run if it had not hit the cable, while Murphy thought it would have gone foul. "We joked about it at the umpire meeting today about what would happen if the ball hit the roof," Stammen said afterward. "And it was unlikely, but it happened. The rule is if they deemed the ball to be fair and it comes down you can catch it. If it hits off the roof foul, then it's a foul ball. So they ruled that it hit the roof fair and the outfielder caught it. "Unfortunately, a bad break for us," Stammen said. "Looked like it was a possible home run. Just didn't go our way. Second time that's happened this year to the Padres." Murphy said from his vantage point, the ball wouldn't have stayed fair for a homer. "It was going to be a foul ball for sure," Murphy said. "I'm standing right on that line, a hitter that talented." Chourio, who hit a game-tying, two-run homer earlier in the game, said he was just trying to make sure he made the play. "I wasn't all that sure of what the rule was, and I wasn't really all that sure that it actually did hit anything," Chourio said through an interpreter. "I thought I had a chance on that ball kind of the whole time off the bat. Then the only thing I kind of realized, it changed direction a little bit, but I thought I had a bead on it for the majority of the time." But, if it did change direction, Murphy was pretty sure he knew why. "I'm telling you, Ueck reached up there and knocked that ball down like a basketball center rejecting a ball, you know what I mean?" Murphy said. "I think Ueck was involved." --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Latvian PM on track to lead pro-Ukraine coalition after election win
item.description: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs was set to retain power and form a pro-Ukrainian coalition after his centrist United List secured the biggest parliamentary election victory since Latvia regained independence in 1991.
item.dc:creator: Andrius Sytas
item.content:encoded: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs was set to retain power and form a pro-Ukrainian coalition after his centrist United List secured the biggest [USN:L8N45O1BP TEXT:"parliamentary election"] victory since Latvia regained independence in 1991. With 97% of ballots counted after Saturday's election in the NATO and European Union country bordering Russia, United List was on 35.3%, enough for 42 seats in the 100-seat parliament. A businessman and amateur rally driver, Kulbergs, 47, came to power in May after the previous coalition crumbled over its handling of incidents in which stray [USN:L8N41K055 TEXT:"Ukrainian military drones"] flew undetected into Latvia. Latvia's economy has underperformed its Baltic neighbours for more than a decade and Kulbergs has vowed to improve governance, cut red tape and reduce public spending, political scientist Roberts Kits said. "Kulbergs played on being a get-things-done type of guy and has persuaded the voters that he can do things differently, bring some fresh energy," he said. "This means the responsibility is huge. People expect him to deliver, but the question remains whether he has the team to do it." United List appeared able to secure a parliamentary majority with either the nationalist National Alliance or the liberal Progressives, Kits said. PM PLEDGES TO MAINTAIN HARD LINE ON RUSSIA Kulbergs pledged continuing support to Ukraine and to keep a hard line towards Moscow. "Any economic ties with Russia makes us weak. Yes, it can bring some extra money, but it's a weakness Russia might exploit," he told reporters at his party's headquarters on election night as supporters celebrated the scale of the win. "It's remarkably good. I was not expecting such a result," Kulbergs said. Voter turnout was 51.8%, down from 59.4% in 2022. United List was followed by the populist, MAGA-style Latvia First, which was on 13.1%. Latvia First had courted the country's substantial ethnic Russian minority in the run-up to the vote. Third in the ranking was the pro-Russian Sovereign Power party, on 11.7%, followed by the National Alliance, which promotes a hardline approach to the Kremlin, at 8.9%. Throughout his campaign, Kulbergs promised more anti-drone capability for Latvia and to maintain defence spending at 5% of gross domestic product, one of the highest levels in NATO. His pro-Kremlin rivals said Latvia should stop any aid to Ukraine and instead focus on tackling cost-of-living issues, particularly among the country's Russian-speaking minority. Although pro-Russian parties increased their representation, Kits said they remained sidelined and were unlikely to influence government policy. Latvia's ethnic Russian minority is split between those who oppose Moscow's war in Ukraine and others who voice frustration with policies at home aimed at limiting their influence on public life, which many of them see as discriminatory. Latvia, with a population of 1.9 million, is sandwiched between the Baltic Sea and Russia and Belarus to the east, with EU and NATO allies Estonia and Lithuania to the north and south.

item.title: Dodgers will continue going left with Blake Snell in Game 2 against Braves
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Dodgers will open their National League Division Series with a double dose of left-handers.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Dodgers will open their National League Division Series with a double dose of left-handers. After Tarik Skubal dominated in Game 1 for the Dodgers, it will be Blake Snell to take the mound for Game 2 against the visiting Atlanta Braves on Sunday. The decision leaves Los Angeles ace and 2025 postseason hero Yoshinobu Yamamoto to pitch in Game 3 of the best-of-five series on Tuesday at Atlanta. "You can put those three or four (starters) in a hat and kind of make a decision," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of his rotation. "... I think just kind of looking out potentially, that just sets up the rotation and Yamamoto better looking forward." The Braves have not committed to a Game 2 starter, but are considering their own left-hander in Chris Sale, who recorded the final four outs against the Philadelphia Phillies in the deciding Game 3 of their NL wild-card series on Thursday. "We still haven't decided yet," Braves manager Walt Weiss said after the 5-3 road loss in Game 1 on Saturday. "... We'll have some conversations about this. So not sure who's going to start. That's where we're at right now." As for facing a left-handed starter for the second time in two games, Weiss was hardly surprised that another opponent elected to focus more on his left-handed hitters like Matt Olson, Drake Baldwin and Michael Harris II. "We're used to it," Weiss said. "Everyone lines up their lefties against us. It's happened all year. It's happened with starters. It's happened with the opposing bullpen. Even during the year, they'd call up lefties for the series." The plan worked well for the Dodgers on Saturday when Skubal opened by allowing one hit over five scoreless innings. A Los Angeles offense that struggled for two months after the All-Star break received home runs from Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy. Hernandez rebounded from a sub-par July and August with a .341 batting average in September. Tucker struggled in the first year of a four-year, $240 million contract but his six September home runs were his most in any month. "Obviously, we've been going through a lot this year, but we stayed together," Hernandez said when asked about watching Tucker hit his home run. "We have each other's back. We're going to continue to try to do our best and try to do our job so we can keep winning." Snell went 4-1 with a 1.90 ERA in nine starts during an injury-marred season when he had left shoulder fatigue, loose bodies in his elbow and late-season groin soreness. In six career regular-season starts against the Braves, he is 0-3 with a 3.49 ERA. "I think the coolest part about the whole group that no one gets to see is really how much we talk about pitching," Snell said about the Dodgers' rotation. "It's very unique. It doesn't happen everywhere. For all of us to kind of be pushing for each other to be great, it's a really cool starting staff to be a part of." Amid a daunting task, the Braves head into Game 2 with some momentum after Ozzie Albies hit a two-run home run in the ninth inning Saturday and the tying run came to the plate late in the game. "I think anytime the other team feels you and has to go to leverage guy after leverage guy, in the end it always helps for the next day," Braves reliever Brent Suter said about the Dodgers using pitchers Tanner Scott and Evan Phillips in the ninth inning. --Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.title: Bahrain Grand Prix in Sepang delayed due to heavy rain
item.description: The start of the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was delayed on Sunday due to heavy rain at the Sepang International Circuit. The race was due to start at 3 p.m. (0700 GMT).
item.dc:creator: Rohith Nair
item.content:encoded: The start of the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia was delayed on Sunday due to heavy rain at the Sepang International Circuit. The race was due to start at 3 p.m. (0700 GMT). The governing FIA said no improvement is forecasted for the next 10 minutes and sent the medical car out to report on track conditions. The medical car reported a "significant amount of standing water" around the track, with the FIA adding that current conditions were not suitable to start the race. Red Bull's [USN:L1N45P01Z TEXT:"Max Verstappen is on pole position"], his first of the season, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton alongside him on the front row. Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli will start third on the grid.

item.title: Michael King on mound as Padres seek to level NLDS vs. Brewers
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- The San Diego Padres will turn to ace right-hander Michael King on Sunday to try to even their best-of-five National League Division Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- The San Diego Padres will turn to ace right-hander Michael King on Sunday to try to even their best-of-five National League Division Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. King (12-10, 3.21 ERA in the regular season) allowed one hit in seven scoreless innings in an 8-0 wild-card victory over the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday. He will be opposed by Milwaukee rookie right-hander Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47) in Game 2 of the NLDS. The Brewers, who earned home-field advantage throughout the playoffs after a franchise-record 103 victories, rallied to win the series opener 3-2 on Saturday night on William Contreras' tiebreaking solo homer in the seventh. "It always feels good when Michael's on the mound. We felt good when he's on the mound all season," Padres manager Craig Stammen said following Game 1. "He's definitely been our leader on the pitching staff for the entire season, made every start, pitched really well, coming off a great outing against the Cubs in the wild-card series. "We're lucky to have him going into Game 2 and feel really good about it." Milwaukee's bullpen combined for five scoreless innings in the opener after ace Jacob Misiorowski struggled through four innings, allowing two runs on four hits and needing 88 pitches. Jackson Chourio added a tying two-run homer in the third inning for the Brewers. It was the fifth career postseason homer for the 22-year-old Chourio, the most in franchise history. The Brewers were last in the NL with 154 homers, ahead of only the Toronto Blue Jays' 152 in the majors. "I like it that we won that way," Contreras said through an interpreter. "Obviously, there's a lot of people in the public opinion that think that we're not able to connect with the big hits, with the homers. "I like that today that's how the game shook out and we were able to win like that. And we were able to show that we were able to play that game as well." San Diego, which won 17 of its final 20 games before sweeping the Cubs in the wild-card series, left 12 runners on base and was just 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position in the opener. King is 0-2 with a 2.96 ERA in four career starts against Milwaukee. He faced the Brewers once this season, allowing one run in 5 2/3 innings but did not get the decision when the Padres rallied for a 3-1 road win on May 13 with three runs in the ninth. "They're going to try to make us play that Brewer style of baseball," King said Saturday. "And if they can speed it up and speed me up on the mound, then they're gonna win. So, it's all about slowing the game down, making sure that I stay in control and we stay in control as a defense to shut down their, I guess I'll call them antics, but it's just playing baseball well." Henderson, 5-1 with a 1.93 ERA in his final seven starts, said he was ready for his postseason debut despite having just 23 major league starts, including 18 this season. "Not trying to make it too much bigger than it is, and preparing for it like another start," Henderson said Saturday. "And I think we understand the stakes, but you've got to treat it the same. So, yeah, I feel prepared." Henderson took the loss in a 3-2 defeat at San Diego on Aug. 10 when the Padres swept the three-game series. He allowed three runs on five hits in 6 1/3 innings, including homers by Ty France and Jackson Merrill. --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Haunted by grief, Gaza's displaced still wait overseas for return
item.description: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return.
item.dc:creator: Nidal Al-Mughrabi
item.content:encoded: Omar al-Hassayna fled Gaza for Cairo after an Israeli airstrike wiped out much of his large family. Three years on, he remains there waiting for enough stability, security and reconstruction in his still devastated homeland to return. Hassayna is one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war that was triggered by the Hamas attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, and who remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures. They still mourn dead relatives and their [USN:L1N45F09E TEXT:"destroyed homes"] and neighbourhoods. "I left Gaza and came to Egypt, the land of Kinana (referring to Egypt), but at the same time, this will not be forgotten, my dear brother, it will not be forgotten," he said. "I am waiting for the opportunity, I am waiting for the moment when Gaza becomes stable so I can return to my country, and be a productive member of this country, and be a positive force for the country." Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza that was meant to start a process of reconstruction under a technocratic government along with a political process that would lead to an eventual full Israeli withdrawal, little has changed. Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most of the area where Palestinians live, mostly in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies and no prospect of reconstruction soon. Some 308 members of Hassayna's [USN:L8N4400Z0 TEXT:"extended family"] were killed when Israeli strikes destroyed a cluster of Gaza City apartment buildings where they had gathered for shelter on November 22, 2023, according to Palestinian authorities. Among those killed were his wife, four of their adult sons and four small grandchildren including an infant only a few months old. Hassayna's oldest son Mohammed is also in Cairo along with his own four children, as is the widow of one of his dead sons with her daughter. He has brothers in the Egyptian capital too. One daughter was medically evacuated to Turkey with her husband and six children, and another daughter remains in Gaza with her five children although her husband was killed in the attack. The Israeli military did not respond to a request for comment on the details of the November 22 strike. It said its attacks in Gaza are directed at military targets, while trying to reduce harm to civilians. ABOUT 7,000 PALESTINIANS HAVE RETURNED TO GAZA In August, Hassayna watched on video from Cairo as relatives buried 112 family members, including his wife, sons and grandchildren, whose bodies had been recovered from the rubble, with dozens still missing. Hassayna owned a business selling tools for firefighting and safety equipment in Gaza and some of his goods survived the war. He periodically sells some to fund his stay in Cairo, where he has remarried. All those who left Gaza were vetted before their departure by both Israel and Egypt, but many have found it hard to return to the territory. Although some Israeli politicians have urged a policy of encouraging all Gaza's population to leave and to prevent those who left from returning, about 7,000 have gone home. Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza. However, no widespread return of those who fled Gaza may be likely until the territory's prospects are clearer. "If Gaza returns. If there is an international agreement (with) a comprehensive situation for the Palestinian people and construction begins, why would I delay?" he said.

item.title: Revolut's rise to become Europe's $115 billion big bank rival
item.description: Revolut has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Revolut has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees. Yet Revolut faces many hurdles itself, with the amount of revenue it extracts per customer a fraction of its established competitors and a small lending business by industry standards. A spokesperson for Revolut said in an email that the London-based company has a "diversified business model", earning its revenue from various products and services rather than lending. "That means our growth depends on building things customers value, rather than on interest rates," the spokesperson said. Here's Revolut's rise, in five charts: GOING FOR GLOBAL CEO Nik Storonsky has stressed he wants Revolut to be truly global, expanding into markets [USN:L4N44E0AO TEXT:"from Mexico to Australia"]. The company has announced several new licences in recent weeks, as it aims to become one of only a handful of banks with retail operations spanning so much of the globe. Meanwhile, some traditional lenders seen as global, including HSBC (HSBA.L) , are reducing their retail footprint. Valued at $115 billion privately, Revolut is now worth more than Britain's Barclays (BARC.L) and France's Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) as investors bet on its tech platform winning over more customers globally. Revolut's 2025 pretax profit was £1.7 billion ($2.2 billion), a fraction of Barclays' £9 billion, but growing fast. Paulo Macedo, CEO of Portugal's biggest bank, Caixa Geral de Depósitos, said in June that 2025 was the last year in which the 150-year-old bank would record higher profit than Revolut. "When you go to Europe the bank CEOs there are talking about Revolut as their most important threat because of their aggressive marketing and growth," said Cihan Duran, director at S&P Global Ratings. MARRED BY SETBACKS In the US, where Revolut has a provisional license, it will face tougher competition, investors said. "The US could be potentially the biggest growth for Revolut. But at the same time, the US is the most competitive market," said Konstantin Sidorov, CEO of the London Technology Club, which invested in Revolut when it was valued at just $5.5 billion. There have been setbacks, including a fine in Lithuania for failing to prevent money laundering. Revolut said an investigation had not identified any confirmed instances of money laundering, adding that it had signed a settlement with the central bank and taken steps to resolve shortcomings. And in September, Revolut accidentally sent customer data to hackers posing as government investigators. The company said its systems and customer funds were unaffected and it had contacted the "limited number of impacted individuals" to give support. In 2024 and 2025, Revolut was the most-complained-about bank in Britain in fraud cases whereby customers are tricked into sending cash to scammers, Ombudsman data compiled by consumer advocacy firm Which? showed. Revolut has previously said in response it takes fraud very seriously and has robust customer protections in place. CUSTOMERS HAVE SURGED A striking measure of its growth is customer numbers. In Ireland, for example, Revolut said that 80% of the adult population has a Revolut account. Revolut's website shows it has 80 million customers, against 84 million for JPMorgan (JPM.N) and 41 million for HSBC. REVENUE-PER-CUSTOMER IS LOW Revolut makes far less from each of its customers than traditional banks, a Reuters analysis of its figures shows. Average deposit balances are also much lower. Lower per-customer revenue is in part because Revolut lends much less than traditional banks, instead relying on fees such as card subscriptions. With just £2.2 billion in loans at end-2025, Revolut's loan-to-deposit ratio of 6% compares with 55% for HSBC and 86% for Societe Generale. Scaling its lending business will introduce risks including managing big and complex credit exposures, while entering fiercely competitive local mortgage markets will not be easy, analysts and investors said. TOO FEW PRIMARY ACCOUNTS Revolut has attracted customers with its easy-to-use app but executives acknowledge too few use it as a primary bank account. Revolut declined to comment in its latest results on how many customers did so in 2025, but said the figure was up 45% from a year ago. This metric is a focus for Revolut's biggest backers. Alex Immerman, an investor at Andreessen Horowitz, which is known as "a16z", told Reuters it was watching for primary-account adoption, as well as total customer balances. ($1 = 0.7573 pounds)

item.title: NHL roundup: Penguins cede 4-goal lead, sink Canadiens in OT
item.description: Tommy Novak scored two goals, including the game-winner at 1:33 of overtime, to give the Pittsburgh Penguins, who relinquished a four-goal lead, a wild 6-5 victory over the visiting Montreal Canadiens on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tommy Novak scored two goals, including the game-winner at 1:33 of overtime, to give the Pittsburgh Penguins, who relinquished a four-goal lead, a wild 6-5 victory over the visiting Montreal Canadiens on Saturday night. Evgeni Malkin, who finished with a goal and two assists, crossed a pass past Montreal defenseman Mike Matheson to Novak at the bottom of the right circle on a 2-on-1 break and Novak roofed a wrist shot over goaltender Jakub Dobes. Erik Karlsson and Kris Letang each had two assists and Ben Kindel, Declan Carlile and Samuel Girard also scored goals for Pittsburgh, which routed rival Philadelphia on Wednesday in its season opener. Arturs Silovs made 20 saves. Sidney Crosby had an assist, the 1,109th of his career, moving him into a tie with Joe Thornton for seventh in NHL history. Nick Suzuki had a goal and three assists, Cole Caufield scored two goals, Chris Kreider and Ivan Demidov each had a goal and an assist for Montreal, which beat rival Toronto on Tuesday in its season opener. Dobes finished with 24 saves. Hurricanes 3, Flyers 2 (OT) Shayne Gostisbehere scored a power-play goal in overtime to lift Carolina to its first win of the season over host Philadelphia. Gostisbehere's decisive goal was a one-timer from the top of the left circle at 2:51 of the extra session. Pyotr Kochetkov made 16 saves to earn the win for the Hurricanes. The defending champions' first two goals came courtesy of Sebastian Aho, including one 10 seconds into the contest. Owen Tippett and Matvei Michkov scored for the Flyers, who were swept by Carolina in the Eastern Conference semifinals last season. Joseph Woll turned aside 37 shots for the hosts, who remain winless in three games this season. Sharks 5, Kings 4 (OT) Igor Chernyshov scored twice, including the overtime winner, as San Jose edged the visiting Los Angeles. Chernyshov, who also had an assist in regulation, one-timed a Macklin Celebrini feed under Anton Forsberg's arm for the game-winner with 1:42 remaining in the extra frame. Tyler Toffoli, Kiefer Sherwood and Nolan Allan also scored while Yaroslav Askarov made 31 saves. Adrian Kempe, Quinton Byfield and Artemi Panarin each scored and added an assist, and Erik Haula also scored a goal for the Kings. Brandt Clarke chipped in two assists and Forsberg stopped 20 shots. Lightning 3, Capitals 1 Reigning Vezina Trophy winner Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 shots in his 600th career game, and Tampa Bay won for the first time this season by topping visiting Washington. Jake Guentzel had a goal and an assist, and Charle-Edouard D'Astous and Conor Geekie also found the net as Tampa Bay evened its record through two matches. Brandon Hagel had two assists. Justin Sourdif scored for the Capitals, who lost the second part of their weekend back-to-back set. Goaltender Charlie Lindgren made 27 saves for Washington, and teammate Dylan Strome skated in his 600th game. Sabres 4, Blackhawks 3 After missing most of last season with a blood clot, Jiri Kulich scored the game-winning goal with 6:40 remaining in regulation to propel Buffalo to a victory in its home opener over Chicago. Tage Thompson tallied a goal and an assist, and Jack Quinn and Rasmus Dahlin also scored for the Sabres, while Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 12 saves. Ryan Donato, Tyler Bertuzzi and Oliver Moore scored for the Blackhawks. Anton Frondell and Alex Vlasic finished with two assists apiece, while Spencer Knight stopped 24 shots as Chicago opened its season with three straight losses, all on the road. Mammoth 4, Blue Jackets 1 Nick Schmaltz scored twice to lead visiting Utah to win over Columbus. Dylan Guenther had a goal and two assists and defenseman Mikhail Sergachev a goal and an assist for the Mammoth. Clayton Keller and Logan Cooley had two assists each and Sebastian Cossa, in his first NHL start, made 17 saves. Utah has outscored opponents 10-1 in its first two games of the season. Kent Johnson got the goal for the Blue Jackets and Jet Greaves stopped 27 shots. Oilers 3, Kraken 1 Leon Draisaitl scored the tiebreaking goal with 2:27 remaining to give Edmonton a victory against visiting Seattle. Connor McDavid added an empty net goal with 1:05 left to clinch the victory. Owen Michaels also scored and goaltender Devon Levi made 19 saves as the Oilers won their second straight after a season-opening 6-5 overtime loss to visiting Vancouver. Bobby McMann tallied for the Kraken and Philipp Grubauer stopped 22 of 24 shots. Senators 3, Maple Leafs 2 Stephen Halliday scored the tiebreaking goal midway through the third period and visiting Ottawa won its season opener, defeating Toronto. Newly appointed captain Thomas Chabot had a goal and assist and Michael Amadio also scored for Ottawa. Claude Giroux added two assists and Linus Ullmark stopped 27 shots. Auston Matthews and Kirill Marchenko scored for the Maple Leafs, who have lost two of their first three games, all of which have been at home. Sergei Bobrovsky made 26 saves for Toronto. Predators 2, Stars 1 First-period goals by Steven Stamkos and Nils Hoglander held up to the final buzzer as host Nashville claimed a victory over Dallas for its first win of the season. Goaltender Juuse Saros made 29 saves -- 12 in the third period -- for the Predators, who rebounded after opening the campaign with a home loss to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday. Stamkos' goal was the 625th of his career, tying him with Joe Sakic and Jarome Iginla for 17th on the NHL's all-time goals list. Miro Heiskanen scored for the Stars, who have dropped two consecutive games to begin the season. Goalie Casey DeSmith stopped 24 shots and was denied the 100th victory of his career. Islanders 6, Devils 0 Simon Holmstrom, Brayden Schenn and Bo Horvat scored within a nine-minute span in the second period and goalie Ilya Sorokin stopped all 37 shots he faced for New York, which won its home opener by routing New Jersey. Victor Eklund, Ondrej Palat and Casey Cizikas scored in the third for the Islanders. Reigning Calder Trophy winner Matthew Schaefer had two assists. The shutout for Sorokin was the franchise-record 30th of his career. Nico Daws made 26 saves for the Devils, who have split their first two games. Wild 4, Bruins 1 Kirill Kaprizov scored a pair of goals and Minnesota pulled away after a slow start for a win over Boston in Saint Paul, Minn. Quinn Hughes tallied a goal and an assist for the Wild, who won their second game in a row to start the season. Team captain Jared Spurgeon also scored a goal, and goaltender Jesper Wallstedt stopped 26 of 27 shots in the victory. Tanner Jeannot scored the lone goal for the Bruins, who were playing on short rest after defeating the host Winnipeg Jets in overtime one night earlier. Goaltender Michael DiPietro allowed three goals on 29 shots in his season debut. Avalanche 6, Blues 1 Martin Necas had two goals and added an assist, Nathan MacKinnon had three assists and Colorado comfortably beat St. Louis in Denver. Nicolas Roy, Artturi Lehkonen and Josh Manson had a goal and an assist each and Cale Makar also scored for Colorado, which is off to a fast start this season with 14 goals through two games. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves and Parker Kelly had two assists for the Avalanche. Dalibor Dvorsky scored for the second straight night for the Blues, who were playing the second game of a back-to-back after winning 4-0 at Dallas on Friday night. Jordan Binnington turned away 30 shots but had two costly turnovers that led to goals. Canucks 4, Flames 1 Defenseman Elias Pettersson scored the go-ahead goal as Vancouver rallied with four unanswered goals in the third period to beat visiting Calgary. Liam Ohgren had a goal and an assist, while Drew O'Connor and Aatu Raty also scored for the Canucks, who earned their first home win. Tom Willander and Linus Karlsson each had two assists while Leevi Merilainen stopped 23 of 24 shots. Matt Coronato scored and Devin Cooley stopped 22 shots for the Flames, who led for most of the game but have lost back-to-back games to begin the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: South Korean president orders probe into data leaks across financial industry
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ordered a thorough investigation and response measures over recent personal data leak incidents at banks, finance companies and public agencies, Seoul's presidential office said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung ordered a thorough investigation and response measures over recent personal data leak incidents at banks, finance companies and public agencies, Seoul's presidential office said on Sunday. Financial Services Commission (FSC) Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting with financial industry associations, regulators and executives from affected institutions on Sunday, warning that the sector must respond with the highest level of vigilance, the FSC said in a statement. The FSC's Lee said authorities could not rule out the possibility that artificial intelligence was used in the attacks and called for an "AI attacks defended by AI" approach, while also signalling broader upgrades to the financial sector's cybersecurity framework. Sunday's meeting came after similar talks on Friday, when the FSC [USN:L1N45O09J TEXT:"said"] Shinhan Bank, KB Kookmin Bank and others had reported cyberattacks, while Yonhap news agency reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank had also suffered breaches. The banks could not immediately be reached for comment outside regular working hours on Sunday. The financial regulator said authorities had launched on-site investigations after Shinhan Bank reported a breach on September 30 and had since expanded probes into other reported incidents. The regulator directed financial institutions to carry out comprehensive security inspections, tighten access controls, minimise external system access and strengthen consumer protection measures. It also said attack methods, internet protocol addresses and other threat information would be rapidly shared across the industry to prevent further incidents. Yonhap news agency said regulators believe the attacks may have broadly scanned multiple financial companies for vulnerabilities rather than targeting a single institution. Attack traffic was reported to have originated from IP addresses across several countries including the United States, Japan, Singapore, Vietnam and Britain, Yonhap said, citing bank data submitted to lawmakers. Sunday's emergency meeting was brought forward from October 7 after additional breaches were discovered at second-tier financial institutions, according to multiple Korean media reports. The country's main opposition People Power Party said authorities should also investigate the possibility of North Korean involvement, citing past cyberattacks attributed to Pyongyang against South Korean financial institutions.

item.title: Despite logistical problems, OCA says Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are a success
item.description: The Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) said on Sunday that a near 20% jump in revenue, strong viewership figures and a slew of world records proved the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games were a success, despite logistical problems plaguing the multi-sport showpiece.
item.dc:creator: Amlan Chakraborty
item.content:encoded: The Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) said on Sunday that a near 20% jump in revenue, strong viewership figures and a slew of world records proved the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games were a success, despite logistical problems plaguing the multi-sport showpiece. The number of participants ballooned to 17,000 following a flurry of late entries — around 2,000 more than projected. With no dedicated Athletes' Village, participants were housed in a mix of hotels, container-style living units and a cruise ship. Satoshi Murate, secretary general if the organising committee, apologised after the unexpected increase strained accommodation and [USN:L6N45L098 TEXT:"transport"] networks, prompting [USN:L6N45I01S TEXT:"complaints"] from athletes and team officials over cramped rooms and small beds. However, OCA Director General Husain Al-Musallam pointed to the 54 world, 11 junior world and 89 continental records set at the Games as evidence of effective organisation. "This achievement does not come without the best environment," the Kuwaiti, who is also president of World Aquatics, told reporters at a press conference on the final day of the Games. "The athletes cannot perform if they don't have transportation. The athletes cannot perform if they don't have good healthcare. The athletes cannot perform if they don't eat food. Number talks, it's evidence. We are here to present you the evidence." He added that at a time when the Games must be sustainable and financially viable, the Aichi-Nagoya model was one worth copying. "We are happy to see that there is no big financial burden in the organising committee, and there is no white elephant staying in Nagoya or any place." The revenue increase, measured against the Games in Hangzhou three years ago, came mainly from digital growth and stronger viewership figures, with India's hockey and cricket matches against Pakistan drawing large TV audiences, OCA officials said. Al-Musallam also said the Games had provided a moment of unity during a time of geopolitical turmoil. "When you look to the news, conflict everywhere - in Asia, outside Asia," he said. "Economic problems everywhere. But look at Asia, how united we are in sport." Tayyab Ikram, chairman of the Games Coordination Committee, acknowledged the logistical problems but said they had overcome them by working together. "There is no Games without challenges. There is no Games without initial interruptions," said Ikram, who also heads the International Hockey Federation. "In future, we would like to see more sustainable solution, more improvement and innovation ... but without compromising on the athletes' conditions."

item.title: ラトビア議会選、首相率いる親ウクライナの与党が勝利
item.description:
Andrius Sytas Terje Solsvik
[リガ ４日 ロイター] - ラトビアで３日に実施された総選挙は、親ウクライナ・中道のクルベルグス首相率いる「連合リスト」が予想を上回る大差で勝利した。開票速報で明らかになった。ロシアによる攻撃の可能性に対する警戒が高まる中、多くの有権者が緊張感を抱えながら投票に臨んだ。
開票率８８％の時点で、連合リストの得票率は３６．６％。ポピュリスト政党「ラトビア・ファースト」
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrius Sytas　Terje Solsvik

[リガ ４日 ロイター] - ラトビアで３日に実施された総選挙は、親ウクライナ・中道のクルベルグス首相率いる「連合リスト」が予想を上回る大差で勝利した。開票速報で明らかになった。ロシアによる攻撃の可能性に対する警戒が高まる中、多くの有権者が緊張感を抱えながら投票に臨んだ。

開票率８８％の時点で、連合リストの得票率は３６．６％。ポピュリスト政党「ラトビア・ファースト」 が１３．４％で続いた。ラトビア・ファーストは選挙戦で、国内に多く暮らすロシア系市民の支持取り込みを図っていた。

バルト諸国はこの数カ月、ロシアがウクライナ支援の切り崩しと社会不安の醸成を狙って、欧州各地で破壊工作やサイバー攻撃などのハイブリッド攻撃を仕掛けていると警告してきた。ロシア側は、こうした非難には根拠がないと反発している。

クルベルグス氏は３日夕、リガにある党本部で、「驚くほどよい結果だ。ここまでとは予想していなかった」と述べ、首相続投に意欲を示す一方で、ラトビア・ファーストとの連立は望まないと述べた。開票速報の結果によれば、組閣には連立が必要となる。

出口調査で３位となったのは親ロシア派の「主権」で得票率は１１．６％。ロシアに対する強硬路線を掲げる右派政党「国民連合」が９．１％で続いた。

item.title: Marquez wins Japanese GP to cut Martin's lead
item.description: Ducati's Marc Marquez won his fourth Japanese Grand Prix to complete a sprint-race double at the Motegi Circuit on Sunday and cut title rival Jorge Martin's championship lead to two points.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ducati's Marc Marquez won his fourth Japanese Grand Prix to complete a sprint-race double at the Motegi Circuit on Sunday and cut title rival Jorge Martin's championship lead to two points. After several riders experienced extreme degradation of their soft rear tyres during Saturday's sprint, the entire grid opted for hard rear tyres and the first few laps of the race were a cagey affair. Polesitter Martin managed to hold on to his advantage off the line and appeared comfortable in the opening eight laps as Marquez waited for the perfect moment to pounce. That opportunity came on the 11th lap when Martin left a sliver of space on his inside, which Marquez exploited to take the lead. The reigning champion then controlled the race to the chequered flag, finishing ahead of Aprilia's Martin and Marco Bezzecchi. "The race was tough, especially when I was behind Jorge, but I knew that if I was able to lead the race, my pace was good," Marquez said. "Jorge tried to attack, but then I just increased a bit more the pace and it was enough to do the last two laps more relaxed." Martin is on 333 points, ahead of Marquez on 331, with six rounds remaining in the season. "I wanted to win but I think today it was really difficult to beat Marc," Martin said. "I rode almost perfectly. I was really smooth, really confident and even then I couldn't win." Martin's teammate Bezzecchi also kept his slim title hopes alive, fending off a late charge by Tech3's Enea Bastianini to finish third. LCR Honda's Diogo Moreira, who clinched his [USN:L1N45P01G TEXT:"first-ever podium on Saturday"] , crashed out, as did Gresini's Alex Marquez after serving a double long lap penalty for his role in a three-rider collision during the sprint. Japan's Ai Ogura (Trackhouse) finished sixth after a thrilling battle with teammate Raul Fernandez and KTM's Pedro Acosta.

item.title: Canucks keep Flames winless with 4-goal third period
item.description: Defenseman Elias Pettersson scored the game-winning goal as the Vancouver Canucks rallied with four unanswered goals in the third period to beat the visiting Calgary Flames 4-1 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Defenseman Elias Pettersson scored the game-winning goal as the Vancouver Canucks rallied with four unanswered goals in the third period to beat the visiting Calgary Flames 4-1 on Saturday. Liam Ohgren had a goal and an assist, while Drew O'Connor and Aatu Raty also scored for the Canucks, who earned their first home win. Tom Willander and Linus Karlsson each had two assists while Leevi Merilainen stopped 23 of 24 shots. Matt Coronato scored and Devin Cooley stopped 22 shots for the Flames, who led for most of the game but have lost back-to-back games to begin the season. The Canucks got off to another slow start and were outshot 11-5 in the first period. They have been outshot 38-12 and have scored just one goal in the opening period of their first three games this season. Coronato opened the scoring at 14:51 of the first period on the power play with a long shot that beat Merilainen cleanly over the right shoulder. Ohgren tied it 1-1 early in the third on a goal that had to be confirmed by a lengthy video review. Ohgren broke in on net, took a shot and then got his own rebound. Cooley got a piece of the shot, but the puck rolled behind him, and he trapped it with his glove hand after it had crossed the goal line. Pettersson backhanded a shot past Cooley at 9:04 of the third period to make it 2-1 and give Vancouver its first lead. O'Connor scored with a wrist shot from the right wing to make it 3-1 at 16:33 and Raty sealed the win just 43 seconds later with a goal into an empty net. This was the teams' first of four meetings. Calgary went 2-1-0 against Vancouver in 2025-26. Both teams return to action Sunday as Vancouver hosts Vegas and Calgary visits Seattle. --Field Level Media

item.title: MLB roundup: Rays flirt with no-hitter, blank Yankees in ALDS opener
item.description: Drew Rasmussen did not allow a hit through 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda belted a solo homer, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 1-0 victory over the New York Yankees on Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Drew Rasmussen did not allow a hit through 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda belted a solo homer, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 1-0 victory over the New York Yankees on Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series in St. Petersburg, Fla. Austin Wells broke up Rasmussen's no-hit bid in the eighth with a blast down the right field line. However, he was thrown out in his attempt to stretch a double into a triple to end the inning. That was the lone hit allowed by Rasmussen (1-0), who struck out 10 batters and walked two in eight innings. Right-hander Bryan Baker struck out two batters in a 1-2-3 ninth. Aranda belted a solo homer off Yankees starter Gerrit Cole (0-1) in the third inning as one of the five hits for the Rays, who secured a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five series. Game 2 is Monday in St. Petersburg. Cole permitted one run on five hits in five innings. Brewers 3, Padres 2 William Contreras homered with two outs in the seventh inning for the go-ahead run to lift Milwaukee to a comeback victory over visiting San Diego in the opener of their National League Division Series. Reliever Adrian Morejon (0-1) opened the seventh and retired the first two hitters before Contreras hit a 406-foot homer to center. Jackson Chourio also homered for the Brewers, his fifth career postseason homer to break the franchise record. Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski needed 88 pitches to get through four innings, allowing two runs on four hits with six strikeouts. Brewers closer Trevor Megill escaped an inherited jam in the eighth and pitched a scoreless ninth to secure the save, catching a break with a deep flyball which ricocheted off the roof and was caught in left by Chourio. The Padres scored their only two runs in the second inning on an RBI single from Luis Campesano and on a fielder's choice to first. Robbie Ray allowed two runs on four hits in his start, which lasted 2 2/3 innings. San Diego stranded the bases loaded in the seventh, when D.L. Hall (1-0) induced a flyout, and left runners on the corners in the eighth. Game 2 is Sunday in Milwaukee. Dodgers 5, Braves 3 Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and Los Angeles opened its NLDS with a victory over visiting Atlanta. Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy all went deep as the Dodgers started their quest to become the first National League club to win three consecutive championships and the first major league team to do it since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000. Skubal (1-0) gave up one run on two hits in his first postseason start for Los Angeles. Sean Murphy and Ozzie Albies hit home runs for the Braves, who entered off a wild-card round victory over the Philadelphia Phillies. Left-handed opener Dylan Dodd opened the game with three scoreless innings for Atlanta before giving way to Victor Mederos (0-1), who gave up Hernandez's home run and recorded just one out in the fourth inning. Game 2 is Sunday evening in Los Angeles. White Sox 3, Guardians 0 Munetaka Murakami belted a two-run homer off All-Star Parker Messick and five pitchers combined on a three-hitter as Chicago beat host Cleveland in their ALDS opener. Murakami, a 26-year-old rookie from Japan, hammered a 440-foot shot to right field off Messick in the fourth inning. His first postseason homer -- and 36th overall this year -- plated Miguel Vargas. Chicago extended its lead to 3-0 in the seventh when Colson Montgomery doubled just inside third base against Erik Sabrowski, bringing home Kyle Teel. The White Sox have won three consecutive games to begin their postseason. Game 2 of the best-of-five series is Monday afternoon in Cleveland. The White Sox have won eight of the 14 contests between the teams this season, splitting eight games at Progressive Field, the home of the AL Central champion Guardians. --Field Level Media

item.title: Igor Chernyshov's OT goal lifts Sharks past Kings
item.description: Igor Chernyshov scored twice, including the overtime winner, as the San Jose Sharks edged the visiting Los Angeles Kings 5-4 on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Igor Chernyshov scored twice, including the overtime winner, as the San Jose Sharks edged the visiting Los Angeles Kings 5-4 on Saturday night. Chernyshov, who also had an assist in regulation, one-timed a Macklin Celebrini feed under Anton Forsberg's arm for the game-winner with 1:42 remaining in the extra frame. Tyler Toffoli, Kiefer Sherwood and Nolan Allan also scored while Yaroslav Askarov made 31 saves as the Sharks picked up their second overtime win in as many games to open the season. Toffoli added an assist and Celebrini finished with a pair of assists. Adrian Kempe, Quinton Byfield and Artemi Panarin each scored and added an assist, and Erik Haula also scored a goal for the Kings, who have dropped a pair of games to open the season. Brandt Clarke chipped in two assists and Forsberg stopped 20 shots. Chernyshov gave San Jose a 4-2 lead at 4:08 of the third, beating Forsberg with a backhand on a partial break. The Kings pulled to 4-3 at 10:21 as Haula redirected an Erik Gustafsson point shot past Askarov. Panarin tied it 4-4 at 14:59 of the third, one-timing a Byfield pass past Askarov. San Jose scored three goals in the middle frame to erase a 1-0 deficit and open a 3-1 lead. Toffoli tied it 1-1 at 1:48 of the middle frame on a power play, tapping in a cross-crease feed from Ivar Stenberg, who recorded his first career point with the helper. Sherwood gave the Sharks their first lead of the night at 9:52 when he intercepted a cross-ice pass by the Kings and snapped a shot from the slot past Forsberg. San Jose doubled its lead at 12:32 of the second when Allan snapped a shot under Forsberg's glove. The Kings cut the lead to one with 1.3 seconds remaining in the second as Byfield beat Askarov short-side over the shoulder on a power play. Los Angeles opened the scoring at 15:50 on a power play as Kempe one-timed a cross-ice feed from Panarin blocker side past Askarov for his first of the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bosnia votes Sunday in election that could affect EU bid
item.description: Bosnians vote on Sunday in elections that could affect their European Union membership bid and the influence that the United States and Russia seek over the small Balkan nation.
item.dc:creator: Branko filipovic
item.content:encoded: Bosnians vote on Sunday in elections that could affect their European Union membership bid and the influence that the United States and Russia seek over the small Balkan nation. Voters are casting ballots for the country's central tripartite presidency and national parliament, alongside regional legislative races in its two federal entities. Voter frustration has grown over an economic slowdown, the slow pace of EU entry talks and a lingering political crisis in which the ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities have repeatedly stalled decisions by the weak central government that links them. Bosnia, which has struggled to recover from the bloody 1992-95 war, secured EU candidate status in December 2022 and the green light to open accession negotiations in 2024. Actual talks have not started because domestic political leaders have yet to enact core requirements such as bolstering judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption laws. Preliminary results are expected to be released by the Central Election Commission after polls close at 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) on Sunday. The Bosnian war ended in 1995 with the US-brokered Dayton peace accord, which left the country split along ethnic lines into the Serb-dominated Republika Srpska and the Bosniak-Croat Federation — linked by the central government and tripartite presidency. Many voters in the country of 3.4 million people say they want to move beyond the divisive rhetoric, but the politics appears stuck. Dusan Cvijic, a 76-year-old pensioner from Banja Luka, the largest city of the Republika Srpska, said the government's policies failed. “What has been done so far has been inadequate. People are struggling; life is very hard. There are ways to improve ..., if things are done honestly, to give people a decent life,” Cvijic said. The vote pits rival ethnic parties — the Bosniak SDA, Serb SNSD and Croat HDZ BiH — against multi-ethnic opposition coalitions led by the Social Democratic Party. According to tracking platform Poliwave, the SDA holds a narrow national lead with 21.4%, followed by the SDP on 16.7%. In Republika Srpska, SNSD, the party run by secessionist leader Milorad Dodik, who wants close ties with Serbia and Russia, is ahead with 34.2%. If ethnically based parties prevail and continue their bickering within the central government, which would be the body that would eventually officially join the EU, progress on accession is likely to be stalled further. In the capital, Sarajevo, Ismar Garasljevic, a 51-year-old high school teacher, said: "More than 30 years after the war, the situation is still the same; we are talking about nationalism ... The same faces, the same story, constantly." Voters on Sunday will face redesigned ballots alongside new biometric voter identification and electronic scanners introduced to curb voting fraud. US AND RUSSIAN INFLUENCE Major powers have long sought influence over Bosnia. The EU is seeking to expand its membership across the Balkans, including Bosnia, but Russia is slowing it down, maintaining its support of the Republika Srpska. The US has also sought to gain influence and wants to push for a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N40Y0SF TEXT:"pipeline project"] to import US liquefied natural gas, run by a company with links to the Trump administration, but the EU warned that the company selection lacked competitive transparency. Washington has also clashed with Brussels over the role of the international High Representative, who, under provisions of the Dayton accord, enforces the laws. [USN:L6N41N07W TEXT:"Christian Schmidt"], a former German government minister, resigned in May under pressure from the US.

item.title: Le chancelier allemand à Kyiv pour finaliser un accord sur les drones et débloquer une aide
item.description: Le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz est arrivé à Kyiv dimanche, accompagné de dirigeants d'entreprises du secteur de la défense, afin d'afficher son soutien au président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky alors que la Russie intensifie ses attaques contre l'Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz est arrivé à Kyiv dimanche, accompagné de dirigeants d'entreprises du secteur de la défense, afin d'afficher son soutien au président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky alors que la Russie intensifie ses attaques contre l'Ukraine. Selon des responsables du gouvernement allemand, Friedrich Merz annoncera un ensemble de mesures comprenant le déblocage d'un milliard d'euros d'aide militaire et de 350 millions d'euros pour la réparation des infrastructures énergétiques. Cette visite devrait également permettre de finaliser un accord de production conjointe de différents types de drones. "Je me suis rendu à Kyiv aujourd'hui car l'Ukraine aura besoin de tout notre soutien dans les semaines à venir", a dit Friedrich Merz. Le chancelier a souligné que les forces russes bombardaient des villes, des immeubles résidentiels et des centrales thermiques. "Si la Russie n'est pas arrêtée, tôt ou tard sa machine de guerre se retournera contre nous", a-t-il estimé. "Je dirai aujourd'hui au président Zelensky: 'Vous pouvez continuer de compter sur notre aide", a-t-il ajouté. Le chancelier allemand est accompagnée de la ministre de l'Economie, Katherina Reiche, et d'une délégation économique comprenant des dirigeants de Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, Diehl Defence, Quantum Systems et d'autres entreprises. Friedrich Merz devrait également faire pression sur le gouvernement ukrainien pour qu'il progresse sur les réformes demandées par les partenaires de l'UE, notamment dans la lutte contre la corruption. Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré mercredi, après s'être entretenu par téléphone avec Friedrich Merz, que l'Ukraine finaliserait prochainement un accord conclu avec l'Allemagne pour la production de drones, de missiles et des logiciels associés. L'un des principaux axes de développement devrait être la production rapide de drones antiaériens, que la société allemande Quantum, spécialisée dans les technologies de défense, a testés avec succès. Depuis l'été, la Russie utilise quotidiennement des dizaines de drones d'attaque à réaction à grande vitesse pour cibler des infrastructures civiles et militaires. En avril, Quantum et le fabricant ukrainien WIY Drones ont annoncé la création de Quantum WIY Industries, une coentreprise destinée à produire le drone intercepteur Strila et les technologies de défense aérienne associées. L'accord prévoit également le développement et la production conjoints d'armes d'une portée de plus de 1.000 km que l'Ukraine peut utiliser pour lancer des attaques en profondeur à l'intérieur de la Russie.

item.title: Germany's Merz arrives in Kyiv to finalize drone deal, release aid
item.description: Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv on Sunday, accompanied by CEOs from German defence companies, in a show of support for President Volodymyr Zelenskiy amid escalating Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
item.content:encoded: Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv on Sunday, accompanied by CEOs from German defence companies, in a show of support for President Volodymyr Zelenskiy amid escalating Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities. Merz will announce a package of measures that includes the release €1 billion in military aid and €350 million for repairs in the energy sector, German government officials said. The visit is also expected to finalize a deal for joint production of various kinds of drones. "I travelled to Kyiv today because Ukraine needs all our support in the coming weeks," Merz said, saying that Russian forces were bombing towns, residential buildings and heating plants. "If Russia is not stopped, sooner or later its war machine will turn against us." "I will tell President Zelenskiy today: 'You can continue to count on our help,'" Merz added. The German chancellor is accompanied by Minister for Economic Affairs Katherina Reiche and an economic delegation including executives from Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, Diehl Defence, Quantum Systems and other firms. Merz is also expected to press the Ukrainian government for progress on reforms requested by EU partners, including in the fight against corruption. Zelenskiy said on Wednesday, after speaking to Merz by phone, that Ukraine would soon [USN:L1N44U0N8 TEXT:"finalise the deal"] with Germany for the production of drones, missiles and related software. A key focus is expected to be the rapid production of anti-jet drones, which Quantum, a German defence-technology company, has successfully tested. Since the summer, Russia has used dozens of high-speed jet attack drones daily to target civilian and military infrastructure. In April, Quantum and Ukrainian manufacturer WIY Drones announced the creation of Quantum WIY Industries, a joint venture to produce the Strila interceptor drone and related air-defence technologies. The deal also involves the joint development and production of weapons with a range of more than 1,000 km (600 miles) that Ukraine can use to launch attacks deep inside Russia. Government officials said the increased cooperation would allow money and technology to flow back to the Federal Republic, where weapons are produced and defences against drones targeting critical infrastructure can be strengthened. On Thursday, Merz said Germany would not be intimidated by the rising number of hybrid attacks by Russia on European states. Russia's Foreign Ministry said in a statement on Saturday that Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in Ukraine in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. It warned foreign nationals and diplomatic staff against staying in or travelling to Ukraine. Zelenskiy told Reuters on Saturday his country's armed forces would double down on their attacks on oil refineries in Russia in response to Moscow's "new doctrine" of escalating [USN:L1N45P05A TEXT:"attacks on civilian infrastructure"], which he said was aimed at forcing residents of Kyiv and other cities to flee. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: テニス＝世界ランク1位シナー、マスターズ上海大会欠場を発表
item.description: ［３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３日　ロイター］ - 男子テニスの世界ランキング１位、ヤニク・シナー（２５、イタリア）は３日、長引いている膝のけがの影響で、マスターズ上海大会（７日開幕）を欠場すると発表した。

シナーは７月１２日にウィンブルドン選手権決勝でアレクサンダー・ズベレフ（ドイツ）を下して以来、公式戦でプレーしていない。２０２４年のマスターズ上海大会では、決勝でノバク・ジョコビッチ（セルビア）を下し、優勝した。

シナーはインスタグラムのストーリーズに「残念ながら今年はマスターズ上海大会でプレーできない。上海のファンの前でプレーするのは楽しいだけに、来週プレーできないことを申し訳なく思う」とつづり、「来年会えることを楽しみにしています」と締めくくった。

シナーの今年の成績は４４勝３敗。ウィンブルドンで四大大会５回目の優勝を達成した。

今年のマスターズ上海大会にはディフェンディングチャンピオンのバレンティン・バチェロット（モナコ）、同大会４回優勝のジョコビッチ、世界ランク２位のズベレフ、同３位のカルロス・アルカラス（スペイン）らが出場する。

item.title: ゴルフ＝ロッテ選手権で山下が6位浮上、ティティクル単独首位
item.description: ［３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのロッテ選手権は３日、米ハワイ州エワビーチのホアカレイＣＣ（パー７２）で第３ラウンドを行い、山下美夢有が６位に順位を上げた。

７位でスタートした山下は６バーディー、１ダブルボギー、１ボギーの３アンダー６９でラウンド。通算１２アンダーの２０４とした。同じく７位で出た畑岡奈紗は２アンダー７０で回ったが、通算１１アンダーの９位に後退した。

岩井千怜と笹生優花はともに４アンダーで回り、通算９アンダーの１８位に浮上した。吉田優利と竹田麗央は通算８アンダーの２４位。西郷真央は通算７アンダーの３０位。西村優菜は４２位、櫻井心那は５３位、岩井明愛は６５位となった。

通算１７アンダーに伸ばしたジーノ・ティティクル（タイ）が単独首位。ユン・イナ（韓国）とポリー・マック（ドイツ）が３打差の２位で並んでいる。

item.title: US carrier George H.W. Bush visits Thailand after six-month Middle East deployment
item.description: The US aircraft carrier George H.W. Bush arrived in Thailand's resort island of Phuket on Sunday with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US aircraft carrier George H.W. Bush arrived in Thailand's resort island of Phuket on Sunday with about 4,800 personnel aboard for a rest-and-recreation break after six months supporting US operations in the Middle East. For the last six months, the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier and its strike group supported Operation Epic Fury and the [USN:L8N44N1OO TEXT:"US naval blockade"] in the US Central Command area of responsibility to secure maritime security and stability in the Middle East , according to the US Navy. Phuket is the first port call for the George H.W. Bush Carrier Strike Group since departing Norfolk, Virginia, and Mayport, Florida, in March, the US Navy said in a statement. Sailors will take part in cultural and community activities in Phuket, including sightseeing tours and a U.S.-Thailand soccer match, it said. The carrier anchored offshore, while crew members are expected to come ashore through Phuket Deep Sea Port and spend time on the popular southern resort island from October 4 to 9, local media reported. Some sailors were seen coming ashore by boat. The visit follows a five-day [USN:L6N44U071 TEXT:"port call"] by the US carrier Abraham Lincoln at Laem Chabang in eastern Thailand last month, with about 5,000 sailors and Marines aboard. A local mayor had estimated each US service member from the Lincoln could [USN:L6N44O0H4 TEXT:"spend"] up to 3,000 baht ($89) per day during the visit. Thailand is the United States' only treaty ally in mainland Southeast Asia. ($1 = 33.53 baht)

item.title: Brewers find home-run power, rally past Padres in NLDS opener
item.description: MILWAUKEE -- William Contreras homered with two outs in the seventh inning for the go-ahead run to lift the Milwaukee Brewers to a 3-2 comeback victory over the San Diego Padres in a battle of the bullpens on Saturday night in the opener of their National League Division Series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: MILWAUKEE -- William Contreras homered with two outs in the seventh inning for the go-ahead run to lift the Milwaukee Brewers to a 3-2 comeback victory over the San Diego Padres in a battle of the bullpens on Saturday night in the opener of their National League Division Series. Reliever Adrian Morejon (0-1) opened the seventh and retired the first two hitters before Contreras sent a 3-2 pitch 406 feet to center. Jackson Chourio had a game-tying two-run homer in the third off Padres starter Robbie Ray to account for Milwaukee's other runs. The Brewers were last in the NL with 154 homers and next-to-last in the majors, only ahead of Toronto's 152. "I feel like we earned it. I really do," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said. "I take nothing away from our guys. We earned it. We weren't perfect. But we swung the bat pretty darn good." Milwaukee earned a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the postseason after winning a franchise-record 103 games, while San Diego won 17 of its final 20 regular-season games before sweeping the Chicago Cubs this week in their wild-card series. Game 2 is set for Sunday afternoon in Milwaukee. Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski, who led the majors with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts, needed 88 pitches to get through four innings, allowing two runs on four hits with six strikeouts. "To limit him to only four innings tonight was a job well done by our offense," Padres manager Craig Stammen said. "Our offense has been swinging the bats really good, taking great at-bats. They continued that again tonight." Left-hander Ray allowed two runs on four hits in 2 2/3 innings. Chourio brought the Brewers even at 2-all with his fifth career postseason homer, the most in franchise history. Garrett Mitchell opened with a broken-bat single to short and advanced to second base on a groundout. Chourio then lined the first pitch 420 feet to left-center with an exit velocity of 113.3 mph. The Padres loaded the bases with two outs in the seventh, but left-hander DL Hall (1-0) entered and got Jackson Merrill to fly out to left. Down 3-2, San Diego had runners on the corners with two outs in the eighth, but closer Trevor Megill came on and fanned Fernando Tatis Jr. Megill, who had a team-high 30 saves in 33 opportunities, finished with a scoreless ninth for the save. That included a lucky break when a Ty France flyball which may have left the yard for what could have been a go-ahead, two-run homer hit the roof. The ball was caught in fair territory on the left field warning track by Chourio for an out which was upheld after review. "I think the only thing that you could probably figure on the ball that everybody's going to be talking about is that (the late Brewers broadcasting legend Bob Uecker) decided to put his hand on it and swat it down so Chourio could catch it. So thanks, Ueck," Murphy said. After forcing Misiorowski to throw 25 pitches in a scoreless first inning, the Padres scored two runs in a 33-pitch second inning. Xander Bogaerts reached on a one-out infield single and Ethan Salas singled. Luis Campusano followed with an RBI single to right. Salas then scored from third, sliding home ahead of the throw on Jake Cronenworth's fielder's choice bouncer to first. "Anytime you score first in a playoff game you feel really good about it, especially the type of pitching staff we have," Stammen said. "We just got beat by a couple home runs tonight." --Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

item.title: Estados Unidos aprovecha errores defensivos y golea 3-0 a México
item.description: La selección de fútbol de Estados Unidos aprovechó el sábado los errores defensivos de México para golearlo por 3-0 en el llamado "clásico de la Concacaf".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La selección de fútbol de Estados Unidos aprovechó el sábado los errores defensivos de México para golearlo por 3-0 en el llamado "clásico de la Concacaf". En el partido disputado en el State Farm Stadium de Glendale, Arizona, Julian Hall, Cavan Sullivan y Malik Tillman anotaron los goles del triunfo para la selección dirigida por el argentino Mauricio Pochettino. "Está claro que han pasado situaciones, pero hay que estar ahí y forzar los errores, y por supuesto que estoy contento. Por supuesto que sabíamos de la rivalidad y de lo que significa, pero lo más importante es ir creciendo para el futuro, el equipo mostró mucha madurez, en los momentos de dificultad mostró un control emocional", dijo Pochettino en conferencia de prensa tras el partido. México inició dominando el partido y tuvo la primera opción de abrir el marcador a los tres minutos cuando Santiago Giménez quedó frente a la portería en el área chica, pero falló al intentar rematar un pase de Roberto Alvarado. A pesar del dominio de México, Estados Unidos se puso en ventaja en su primera llegada a los 28 minutos, cuando Hall definió de derecha en el área chica al aprovechar un error del portero Raúl Rangel, quien dejó el balón suelto al tratar de cortar un centro de Giovanni Reyna. México tuvo la segunda oportunidad de anotar a los 43 minutos, pero Giménez volvió a mandar su remate por un lado a pesar de quedar sin marca en el área chica después de que el portero Diego Kochen rechazó un potente disparo de Luis Romo. Estados Unidos empezó dominando la segunda parte, y México estuvo cerca de empatar a los 58 minutos con un potente disparo de Alvarado dentro del área que desvió Kochen. El segundo gol de Estados Unidos cayó a los 62 minutos gracias a otro error de Rangel, quien al tratar de iniciar una jugada en las afueras del área, dejó el balón en los pies de Sullivan, quien aprovechó el regalo para definir con un colocado zurdazo. La situación para México se complicó a los 67 minutos con la expulsión de Mateo Chávez, quien vio la tarjeta roja por dar una cachetada al centrocampista Sebastian Berhalter cuando el jugador estadounidense le reclamó una falta previa. Estados Unidos siguió controlando el partido y metió el tercer gol a los 84 minutos con un potente zurdazo de Tillman dentro del área después de ganar el balón cuando el centrocampista Álvaro Fidalgo dio un pase retrasado. De esta manera, México sufrió su primera derrota bajo la dirección técnica de Rafael Márquez, quien fue presentado el 10 de septiembre como estratega de la selección tras haber sido asistente técnico de Javier "Vasco" Aguirre en el pasado Mundial. En sus dos primeros compromisos bajo la tutela de Márquez, México empató por 1-1 ante Colombia y Perú. "Han sido errores muy groseros en los que les regalas estos tres goles al rival, es duro perder de esta manera porque fueron regalos nuestros y no aciertos del rival, pero son errores que obviamente se pueden corregir. Creo que hay cosas buenas que rescatar, pero con la preocupación de hacer autocrítica y reponernos lo más rápido posible porque tenemos otro partido en pocos días", dijo Márquez. El próximo partido de México será el 6 de octubre cuando enfrente a Chile en el Memorial Coliseum de Los Ángeles. En tanto, Estados Unidos jugará ante Canadá.

item.title: Martin Necas' 3 points help Avalanche blast Blues
item.description: Martin Necas had two goals and added an assist, Nathan MacKinnon had three assists, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the St. Louis Blues 6-1 in Denver on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Martin Necas had two goals and added an assist, Nathan MacKinnon had three assists, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the St. Louis Blues 6-1 in Denver on Saturday night. Nicolas Roy, Artturi Lehkonen and Josh Manson had a goal and an assist each and Cale Makar also scored for Colorado, which is off to a fast start this season. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves and Parker Kelly had two assists for the Avalanche, who have scored 14 goals in sweeping their season-opening two-game homestand. Dalibor Dvorsky scored for the second straight night for St. Louis, which was playing the second game of a back-to-back after winning 4-0 at Dallas on Friday night. Jordan Binnington turned away 30 shots and had two costly turnovers that led to goals. The first came after Manson's goal made it 3-0 early in the second period. Binnington tried to clear the puck up the center of the ice, Lehkonen knocked it down in the slot and scored into the open net at 11:40. Colorado put it away with two goals late in the second. Roy's one-timer at 18:02 beat Binnington on the short side. The goaltender's second gaffe, when he misplayed the puck behind the net, led to Necas' second of the night 23 seconds later. Binnington has allowed six goals in each of his last two starts against the Avalanche, with the last coming on New Year's Eve 2025 in Denver. Colorado took the early lead when MacKinnon fed Necas in front of the net, he slid the puck to Makar at the right of the crease, and he lifted it over Binnington's pads at 4:09 of the first. Necas made it 2-0 later in the period when Lehkonen stole the puck in the offensive zone, sent it to MacKinnon, and his cross-zone pass found Necas at the left circle. Necas wristed a shot to the far post at 13:12. Dvorsky spoiled Blackwood's shutout bid when he scored at 2:34 of the third period. --Field Level Media

item.title: Panthers, without injured captain Aleksander Barkov, take on Ducks
item.description: The Florida Panthers go into their third game of the new season with injuries creating the biggest headlines, which was the case during the 2025-26 campaign.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Florida Panthers go into their third game of the new season with injuries creating the biggest headlines, which was the case during the 2025-26 campaign. When the Panthers visit the Anaheim Ducks on Sunday night, they will be without center and team captain Aleksander Barkov, who was placed on long-term injured reserve with a lower-body injury on Saturday. He must miss at least 10 games. Barkov left the second period of Florida's 4-3 overtime loss to the host San Jose Sharks on Thursday after going down awkwardly while battling for the puck. He missed the entire 2025-26 season with ACL and MCL injuries to his right knee sustained on the first day of training camp. Barkov was able to play for Finland in the IIHF World Championship, helping the team win the gold medal in May. The injury on Thursday night appeared to be to his left leg. "It's not related to his injury last year at all," Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after Thursday's game. Maurice told reporters on Saturday that Barkov would return to Florida to be examined by the team's medical personnel to determine the exact nature of the latest injury. Barkov, 31, is a three-time winner of the Selke Trophy as the NHL's top defensive forward and was a key part of the Panthers' Stanley Cup-winning teams in 2024 and 2025. Florida began Thursday's game without defenseman Gustav Forsling due to an upper-body injury. Forsling scored in the Panthers' 1-0 overtime win over the host Carolina Hurricanes in the season opener on Tuesday. Brad Marchand (lower body) is expected to miss the entire month of October due to a surgical procedure in August, and winger Jonah Gadjovich is on long-term injured reserve. He has been out since having neck surgery last November. Maurice said Forsling is a game-time decision on Sunday night. Center Sam Lafferty and defenseman Alexander Petrovic were recalled from AHL Charlotte on Saturday. Eetu Luostarinen scored twice in the loss on Thursday and Matthew Tkachuk added a goal. Akira Schmid made 28 saves in his Panthers' debut. The Ducks are coming off their season opener on Friday night, when they held on for a 4-3 win over the host Vegas Golden Knights, who eliminated Anaheim in the second round of the Western Conference playoffs last season. The Ducks led 4-0 after two periods. "First one done, 83 more to go," said goalie Lukas Dostal, who stopped 27 shots. Leo Carlsson had a goal and an assist Friday for the Ducks. Carlsson, 21, signed a five-year, $90 million offer sheet with the Philadelphia Flyers during the offseason, which Anaheim matched. "I think from the day that we drafted him, we viewed him as a cornerstone piece of our rebuild, and that hasn't changed," Ducks general manager Pat Verbeek said. "We feel that Leo at some point, and I wouldn't say next year, but I think over the course of this contract, is going to show the elite player that he is, and it's going to give us great reasons for why we matched this offer." Carlsson had 29 goals and 67 points in 70 games last season and added four goals and 11 points in 12 playoff games. Beckett Sennecke, Alex Killorn and Jeff Malott also scored for the Ducks on Friday. --Field Level Media

item.title: Japan PM protests to US after Marine arrested on murder suspicion in Okinawa
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered a protest with the United States on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Okinawa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi registered a protest with the United States on Sunday after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and murdering a Japanese woman in Okinawa. Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the southernmost prefecture, on Saturday and taking her wallet and backpack, police said. Ballard denied the allegations, police said. "The occurrence of such an extremely brutal and vicious incident is extremely regrettable," Takaichi said in a statement. "The government of Japan strongly protests to the US side and strongly seeks maximum cooperation with the investigation," as well as the tightening of discipline and thorough measures to prevent a recurrence, she said. The US embassy and the Marine Corps expressed condolences over the incident and said they were cooperating with the Japanese authorities. The Marines said in a statement that the suspect, who is assigned to the III Marine Expeditionary Force and based at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, was in Japanese custody. "The Marine Corps takes these allegations very seriously and expects every Marine to adhere to the highest standards of behavior," it said. Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972.
