item.title: イエメン軍、首都サヌアでフーシ派に空爆実施
item.description: [４日 ロイター] - イエメン軍は４日未明、首都サヌアと北西部サアダで、親イラン武装組織フーシ派
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[４日 ロイター] - イエメン軍は４日未明、首都サヌアと北西部サアダで、親イラン武装組織フーシ派 に対して攻撃を実施していると明らかにした

軍の報道官によると、同軍は「重要目標」と称する標的を攻撃したが、詳細には触れなかった。

フーシ派系のアルマシラＴＶはこれに先立ち、サウジアラビアによるサヌアへの攻撃があったと伝えた。サウジ側からの確認は直ちには得られていない。

イランが支援するフーシ派とサウジが支援する政府軍との紛争は、２０２２年の停戦後ほぼ沈静化していたが、イラン戦争の余波で戦闘が再燃している。

フーシ派は７月にサウジに対する海上封鎖を宣言し、サウジ領土や船舶への攻撃を開始。また、イエメンの紅海沿岸で大幅に勢力域を拡大した。サウジはイエメン政府軍を支援し、同国内のフーシ派拠点に空爆を実施している。

item.title: Drew Rasmussen dominates, Rays stifle Yankees to win ALDS opener
item.description: Drew Rasmussen did not allow a hit through 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda belted a solo homer, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 1-0 victory over the New York Yankees on Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series in St. Petersburg, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Drew Rasmussen did not allow a hit through 7 2/3 scoreless innings and Jonathan Aranda belted a solo homer, lifting the Tampa Bay Rays to a 1-0 victory over the New York Yankees on Saturday in Game 1 of the American League Division Series in St. Petersburg, Fla. "In all honesty, my heartbeat was about a thousand beats per minute, so I just let (catcher) Liam (Hicks) call the game and just try to execute the pitches he called," Rasmussen said on the TNT Sports broadcast. Austin Wells broke up Rasmussen's no-hit bid in the eighth with a blast down the right field line. However, he was thrown out in his attempt to stretch a double into a triple to end the inning. "Obviously not a good decision there," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "Not sure if he saw something on his way between first and second that caused him to go there, but obviously a mistake there." Wells said after he passed second base, he saw third base coach Luis Rojas with his hands up for him to stop there, but he already was committed to run to third. "(They) made two good throws and it got me," Wells said. "Thought it kicked off more than it did, (right fielder Victor Mesa Jr.) made a good play on the ball. Two outs there, trying to make something happen, be aggressive with not much going on in the game. Obviously, love to safe there or standing on second base." That was the lone hit allowed by Rasmussen (1-0), who struck out 10 batters in eight innings. Right-hander Bryan Baker struck out two batters in a 1-2-3 ninth inning to secure his first career postseason save. Aranda belted a solo homer in the third inning as one of the five hits for the Rays, who secured a 1-0 lead in the best-of-five series. Game 2 is Monday in St. Petersburg. Aranda deposited a 2-2 changeup from right-hander Gerrit Cole (0-1) over the wall in right-center field to account for the scoring in the third inning. The Yankees' bats went silent after outscoring the rival Boston Red Sox by an 18-2 margin and out-hitting them 26-7 during a two-game sweep in the wild-card round. Captain Aaron Judge was left off New York's roster for the ALDS. Judge, 34, has not played since Sept. 16 due to a strained right calf. The three-time AL MVP landed on the injured list three days later and missed the Yankees' wild-card sweep earlier this week. Rasmussen also dominated the Yankees in three of four meetings during the regular season, including a one-run, one-hit, 11-strikeout performance over 6 2/3 innings of a 6-1 romp on Sept. 22. The Rays clinched the AL East title with that victory. "At that point, we had the opportunity to win the division. Obviously, this one is a postseason game. Both meaningful, both impactful," Rasmussen told reporters about his last two outings against New York. Rasmussen allowed only a pair of walks, one each in the second and third innings, and retired the final 16 batters he faced on Saturday. "It seemed like he went and doubled down tonight," Rays manager Kevin Cash said, noting Rasmussen's previous start against the Yankees. "Made it easy to sit back and just take some decisions out of our hands." Rasmussen also showed his defensive chops by getting off the mound to field a bunt and throw out Ryan McMahon to begin the sixth inning. He finished that inning unscathed, marking the deepest no-hit bid in franchise history and the deepest into a postseason game the Yankees have ever been no-hit. Cole permitted one run on five hits in five innings. "Biggest issue is Rasmussen shutting us down," Boone said. "Obviously, we had a handful of guys hit some balls on the screws - Austin (Wells) being one of them a couple times there -- we just didn't generate enough, obviously." --Field Level Media

item.title: Poor start for Red Wings can be turned around against Jets
item.description: The Detroit Red Wings' season opener couldn't have gone much worse. They'll look for a better result and more fan support when they host the Winnipeg Jets on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Red Wings' season opener couldn't have gone much worse. They'll look for a better result and more fan support when they host the Winnipeg Jets on Sunday afternoon. Detroit endured a tumultuous offseason in which former captain Dylan Larkin requested a trade and former top executive and franchise legend Steve Yzerman was reassigned to an advisory role. Team owner Chris Ilitch still hasn't hired a permanent replacement for Yzerman, as in-house candidate Shawn Horcoff was named interim general manager prior to training camp. Restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson, one of the team's top defensemen, remains unsigned and returned to his native Sweden earlier in the week as negotiations stalled. Larkin remains on the roster but missed Friday's opener against the New York Rangers with an upper-body injury and won't play on Sunday. He was heavily booed during pregame introductions and chants of "Sell the team," directed at Ilitch, cascaded from the stands at times during Detroit's 2-0 loss. "Obviously he has to live with the ramifications of asking for a trade," coach Todd McLellan said of Larkin. "It's not comfortable for anybody and I feel bad for him, I do." The rest of the players also had to deal with the vitriol from disenchanted fans. "Everyone has a right to express their feelings and we just have to deal with it," defenseman Moritz Seider said after Friday's loss. "We handled it pretty well. Everyone gave it their best shot, and that's what we'll continue to do. You should be professional enough. We get paid to do our job. We have a great opportunity in front of us, to get back to work (Saturday) and prepare ourselves for hopefully our first win in two days." The Red Wings' defense played well without Edvinsson but the offense was punchless without Larkin. "We're going to have to score goals to win games," McLellan said. "The players that we have here, they have to understand and expect it from themselves and their teammates. You just can't rely on three or four guys." The Jets opened their season on Friday with a 4-3 overtime loss to Boston. Winnipeg failed to protect a late 3-2 lead. "I like a lot of what we did. There's mistakes, but we came out strong," said Kyle Connor, who extended his NHL record by scoring in a ninth straight season opener. "We had a little bit of a dip there, and obviously they got one to tie it up. But overall, I thought we played pretty quick." The Jets have a major controversy of their own involving one of their top players. Star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck wants to be traded and didn't report to camp, prompting a suspension. Hellebuyck, like Larkin, is a Michigan native. Stuart Skinner was the starting goaltender on Friday, making 26 saves. Skinner was signed to a two-year deal in July. "I think we were ready. You saw us in the first ten minutes. I think the shots were like eight to one. We were ready to rock and roll. That's just kind of how the game works. There's ebbs and flows of the game," Skinner said. "You know, Boston's definitely going to have their push. We knew that was going to happen. But all in all, I thought we did a really good job and just got to tighten up a few things." --Field Level Media

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝ヤンキース主将ジャッジ、地区シリーズはロースター外
item.description: ［３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）ヤンキースが３日、レイズとの地区シリーズ（５回戦制）の２６人のロースターを発表。主将アーロン・ジャッジ外野手（３４）はメンバーを外れた。

ジャッジは右ふくらはぎの肉離れの影響で９月１６日以降プレーしておらず、その３日後に負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）入り。通算３回のア・リーグＭＶＰ（最優秀選手）選出を誇る同選手は、レッドソックスとのワイルドカードシリーズも欠場した。ヤンキースは同シリーズで２連勝し、地区シリーズに勝ち上がった。

ヤンキースのアーロン・ブーン監督は、ジャッジをロースターに入れなかったことについて「最終的にそれが最善と判断した」とコメント。「彼が復帰に近付いているように感じている」としながらも、「アーロンが本来の状態で復帰し、われわれがワールドシリーズで優勝するためには、あと１週間、彼が復帰に向けて努力を続けることが重要だ」と話した。

さらに同監督は「彼はランニングを始めたばかりで、打撃練習は数日前に再開した。これをさらに数日続けて、持久力を身に付けることが大事」とも述べた。

ジャッジは肋骨の骨折で３カ月以上離脱。９月８日に復帰した後、７試合に出場したが、打率１割７分４厘、１本塁打、３打点とふるわなかった。レギュラーシーズンでは６６試合に出場し、打率２割４分１厘、１８本塁打、４１打点だった。

item.title: サッカー＝欧州ＮＬ、イングランド7得点で大勝 スペイン3連勝
item.description: ［３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）は３日、各地で１次リーグの試合を行い、リーグＡの３組ではイングランドが主将のハリー・ケーンらのゴールでクロアチアに７─０と大勝した。

イングランドは前半８分、ジュード・ベリンガムのパスを受けたケーンが守備陣２枚の間を抜けて先制ゴール。同２１分にベリンガムが決めて加点すると、３─０として迎えた同４５分にベリンガムのクロスからブカヨ・サカがネットを揺らした。

イングランドは後半もケーンとサカのゴールでリードを広げると、同４２分にベリンガムのお膳立てからモーガン・ロジャースにも得点が生まれた。ベリンガムは１試合１ゴール３アシスト。代表通算ゴール数を８９としたケーンは、これが１２４試合目。ピーター・シルトン氏の同代表最多出場記録まであと１試合となった。

同組のスペインはチェコを３─１で破り、開幕から３戦全勝とした。前半６分にラミン・ヤマルがペナルティーエリアの端から左足で強烈なシュートを放つと、同３５分には代表で２年以上ゴールのなかったロドリが決めて２点を先行。後半に１点を失ったが、最後はミケル・メリノのゴールで突き放した。

これにより、同組ではスペインが勝ち点９で首位、イングランドは同６で２位としている。

リーグＢの１組ではスイスがスロベニアを２─１で下して３戦全勝で首位をキープ。スコットランドは北マケドニアを２─０で破り、スロベニアと同じ勝ち点４とした。

item.title: アジア大会＝日本選手団、金メダル83個で60年ぶりに最多更新
item.description: ［３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［３日　ロイター］　 - 愛知・名古屋アジア大会では３日、日本選手団の金メダル数が８３個に到達。これまでの記録を上回り、最多となった。１９６６年バンコク大会で記録した７８を６０年ぶりに更新した。

日本はソフトボール決勝では中国に７─０で快勝し、７連覇を達成。柔道混合団体ではカザフスタンを４─０で下し、３連覇を果たした。ラグビー７人制女子決勝では中国に１０─５で勝利し、８年ぶりの金メダル。水球男子でも優勝した。

セパタクロー男子クワッド（４人制）では日本初の金メダルに輝き、ブレイキン男子では半井重幸（ダンサー名・SHIGEKIX）が２連覇を達成。初採用のパデル、女子ダブルスは塚本早紀、徳本佳恵組が制した。

テニスの混合ダブルスでは柴原瑛菜、フレンド原ジェイ組が青山修子、楠原悠介組をストレートで下して優勝。同大会のテニス競技の決勝が日本人対決となったのは今回が初めてだった。

サッカー男子決勝では日本が韓国に０─１で敗戦。バレーボール男子決勝で、日本はイランにセットカウント１─３で負けた。

日本は今大会、３日の競技を終えた時点で銀メダルは９５個で銅メダルは９１個。金メダルと合わせて２６９個と、３４１個の中国に次ぐ２位のメダル数を記録している。

item.title: PGA club pro Michael Block takes 1-stroke lead after 36 holes in Allentown
item.description: Michael Block needed only 30 shots on the back nine and posted a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Saturday to take a one-stroke lead after two rounds of the inaugural Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic in Allentown, Pa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Michael Block needed only 30 shots on the back nine and posted a bogey-free 7-under 63 on Saturday to take a one-stroke lead after two rounds of the inaugural Jefferson Lehigh Valley Classic in Allentown, Pa. Block, a 50-year-old PGA Tour Champions rookie, stands at 11 under through 36 holes. That puts him one ahead of New Zealand's Steven Alker and two ahead of first-round co-leader Richard Green of Australia. Block, who continues to serve as the head golf professional at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Club in Mission Viejo, Calif., gained a following with a tie for 15th place at the 2023 PGA Championship. Block, who shot a 4-under par 66 on Friday, opened with back-to-back birdies on Saturday. He parred the last seven holes on the front nine, then birdied five of the first seven holes coming in. He is highly appreciative of the welcome he has received on the tour. "So the support I have from the fellow Champions Tour players is amazing," Block said. "The relationships I've gotten in six events/seven, is crazy, and I really appreciate those guys. These guys have been living the Tour life, the PGA Tour life and Champions Tour life for, you know, 20-30 years, and I'm just out here -- and they know my scenario. I'm out here as a club pro, and being out here for my seventh event in my life, and they really support me, which is really cool. Trust me, it helps a lot." In Block's fifth Champions start at The Ally Challenge five weeks ago, he also held the lead after 36 holes. But he was passed by Alker during the final round and ended up tied for third. What did Block learn from that experience? "Yeah, from Ally, just keep being you," he said. "Like, don't try to be the quiet Michael. Quiet Michael doesn't work. Michael having fun works. Michael being quiet, Michael trying to be somebody he's not doesn't work. That's what I'm going to do tomorrow." In contrast to Block, who's happy just to be on the verge of qualifying for the Charles Schwab Cup playoffs, Alker has won three times in 2026, owns 13 PGA Tour Champions titles and ranks No. 3 on the Schwab Cup money list. The 55-year-old has posted matching 65s and, like Block, played bogey-free golf on Saturday. He shot 31 on the inward half and played the par-3's in 2-under. Alker is well aware the gallery will be flocking to Block on Sunday. "He's got a great following and I think the crowds will be good tomorrow and want him to do well," Alker said. "He's a bit different, he likes to talk about things. It's fun. I kind of like watching him play a little bit, see how he goes about the game. Not that I'll take a whole lot of it forward, but I just like watching him play and how he goes about his game. "He's got game, I've got to bring it tomorrow." Ryan Armour fired a 64 to move into fourth at 8-under. Tag Ridings (65), South Korea's Y.E. Yang (69) and Sweden's Robert Karlsson (69) share fifth at 7-under. Yang and Karlsson joined Green atop the leaderboard after the first round. --Field Level Media

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝地区シリーズ開幕、村上が先制2ラン ドジャース大谷1安打
item.description: ［クリーブランド ３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［クリーブランド　３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）のプレーオフ、地区シリーズ（５回戦制）が３日、各地で開幕。ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手はガーディアンズ戦に「４番・一塁」で出場し、四回にポストシーズン初本塁打となる先制２ランを放った。

ライトスタンドに約１３４メートルの一発をたたき込んだ村上は試合後、通訳を介し「準備はできていた。シーズンを通じてこの瞬間に向けて備えてきた」とコメントした。村上は４打数２安打２打点と活躍。ホワイトソックスは３─０でシリーズ初戦を制した。

ドジャースの大谷翔平選手はブレーブス戦に「２番・指名打者」で出場し、４打数１安打。ドジャースは５─３で勝った。先発のタリク・スクバル投手が６回１失点の好投で勝利投手となった。

item.title: México dice que investigación de la FDA sobre la lechuga no identificó la fuente de la contaminación
item.description: El Ministerio de Salud de México dijo el sábado que la investigación de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EEUU (FDA por su sigla en inglés ) sobre el brote del parásito Cyclospora, relacionado con la lechuga iceberg troceada de Taylor Farms en México, no identificó de forma concluyente el origen de la contaminación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Ministerio de Salud de México dijo el sábado que la investigación de la Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de EEUU (FDA por su sigla en inglés ) sobre el brote del parásito Cyclospora, relacionado con la lechuga iceberg troceada de Taylor Farms en México, no identificó de forma concluyente el origen de la contaminación. La Cofepris, el organismo regulador de la seguridad alimentaria de México, señaló que los análisis realizados por su laboratorio nacional de referencia en materias primas, productos terminados y agua de las instalaciones investigadas en relación con el brote dieron negativo para el parásito Cyclospora. El regulador añadió que los resultados ambientales por sí solos no constituyen una prueba concluyente de que los productos agrícolas fueran la fuente de la contaminación. La FDA [USN:L6N45O12Z TEXT:"declaró el viernes"] que había encontrado un fuerte vínculo epidemiológico y de trazabilidad entre el brote y la lechuga iceberg troceada retirada del mercado, producida por Taylor Farms en México, pero señaló que no había pruebas suficientes para determinar cómo se produjo la contaminación. La agencia informó de dos muestras ambientales positivas para Cyclospora en México: una procedente de las aguas residuales que salían de una planta de procesamiento y otra de una zanja de drenaje en una explotación de lechuga iceberg. Los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) declararon el fin del brote el 11 de septiembre. El brote afectó a 12.883 personas en 21 estados, provocó la hospitalización de 570 personas y se relacionó con dos fallecimientos. México afirmó que había cooperado durante toda la investigación, proporcionando información sobre la trazabilidad, inspecciones y muestras, y que continuaría la cooperación técnica con las autoridades sanitarias estadounidenses.

item.title: Mexico says FDA lettuce probe did not conclusively identify contamination source
item.description: Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mexico's Health Ministry said on Saturday that a US Food and Drug Administration investigation into the cyclospora parasite outbreak linked to shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms in Mexico did not conclusively identify the source of contamination. Mexico's food-safety regulator Cofepris said tests conducted by its national reference laboratory on raw materials, finished products and water from the facility investigated in the outbreak were negative for the cyclospora parasite. The regulator added that environmental findings alone do not constitute conclusive evidence that agricultural products were the source of contamination. The FDA said [USN:L4N45O17K TEXT:"on Friday"] it found a strong epidemiological and traceback link between the outbreak and recalled shredded iceberg lettuce produced by Taylor Farms in Mexico, but said there was insufficient evidence to determine how contamination occurred. The agency reported two environmental samples positive for cyclospora in Mexico, one from wastewater leaving a processing facility and another from a drainage ditch at an iceberg lettuce farm. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention declared the outbreak over on September 11. The outbreak sickened 12,883 people in 21 states, hospitalized 570 and was linked to two deaths. Mexico said it cooperated throughout the investigation, providing traceability information, inspections and samples, and would continue technical cooperation with US health authorities.

item.title: -Lula e Flávio travam disputa acirrada e eleição deve ir para 2º turno, mostram pesquisas
item.description: Pesquisas divulgadas neste sábado mostraram uma disputa apertada na corrida presidencial entre os dois principais candidatos, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pesquisas divulgadas neste sábado mostraram uma disputa apertada na corrida presidencial entre os dois principais candidatos, o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que tenta a reeleição, e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). A corrida deve ser decidida apenas no segundo turno, daqui a três semanas, de acordo com os levantamentos. Para um candidato ser eleito no primeiro turno, no domingo, ele precisa ter mais de 50% dos votos válidos, quando não são computados os votos brancos e nulos. Veja o desempenho de Lula e Flávio nos levantamentos divulgados neste sábado: DATAFOLHA Lula - 45% Flávio - 42% Margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. QUAEST Lula - 46% Flávio - 45% Margem de erro de 2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. CNT/MDA Lula - 47,8% Flávio - 42,1% Margem de erro de 2,2 pontos percentuais para mais ou para menos. (Redação São Paulo)

item.title: Lula tem 46% dos votos válidos contra 45% de Flávio Bolsonaro no 1º turno, mostra Quaest
item.description: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão em empate técnico nos votos válidos do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com vantagem numérica de 1 ponto percentual para o petista, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) estão em empate técnico nos votos válidos do primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de domingo, com vantagem numérica de 1 ponto percentual para o petista, mostrou pesquisa Quaest neste sábado. Lula tem 46% dos votos válidos, quando são excluídos os brancos, nulos e indecisos, enquanto Flávio soma 45%. A margem de erro da pesquisa é de 2 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos. Para vencer no primeiro turno no domingo, um candidato precisa ter mais de 50% dos votos válidos. Nos chamados votos totais, o presidente aparece com 40% (eram 39% na pesquisa anterior), contra 38% do senador de oposição (eram 34%). Os indecisos somam 3% (eram 5% na pesquisa anterior), enquanto aqueles que dizem que votarão em branco, anularão o voto ou não votarão em nenhum candidato chegam a 10%, mesma parcela da pesquisa anterior. Já num eventual segundo turno entre os dois, Flávio Bolsonaro aparece numericamente à frente, com 44% (eram 42%), enquanto Lula registra os mesmos 42% do último levantamento.

item.title: NC State RB Jayden Scott (foot) leaves game vs. Louisville
item.description: Jayden "Duke" Scott, North Carolina State's top running back, left Saturday's home game against Louisville early with a lower-body injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jayden "Duke" Scott, North Carolina State's top running back, left Saturday's home game against Louisville early with a lower-body injury. He was later seen on the sideline wearing a boot on his left foot. Scott walked to the locker room after a Wolfpack drive in the first quarter. In his third season in Raleigh, Scott had 346 yards and four touchdowns on 57 carries through the Wolfpack's first four games. He ran five times for 12 yards on Saturday. With Scott out, Davion Gause received the majority of the carries for NC State (2-2, 0-1 Atlantic Coast Conference) through the first three quarters. --Field Level Media

item.title: Reports: Pitt QB Mason Heintschel (knee) done for season
item.description: Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel will reportedly miss the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, multiple outlets reported Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pitt quarterback Mason Heintschel will reportedly miss the rest of the season with a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee, multiple outlets reported Saturday. According to ESPN, Heintschel suffered the injury during Friday night's 35-33 road victory over Virginia Tech. he was scrambling in the third quarter when he took a hit to the knee while being tackled by two Virginia Tech players. The sophomore has passed for 1,304 yards and 14 touchdowns against one interception this season while leading Pitt to its second 5-0 start since 1991. Holden Geriner, a fifth-year quarterback, replaced Heintschel against the Hokies and is the likely starting quarterback when the Panthers host North Carolina on Oct. 10. Heintschel completed 10 of 18 passes for 113 yards and a touchdown before exiting. Geriner went 8 of 12 for 78 yards and one score. Geriner played previously for Auburn (2022-24) and Texas State (2025). He has completed 19 of 26 passes for 219 yards and two touchdowns this season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Top 25 roundup: No. 25 Mizzou runs it up in rout of No. 8 Florida
item.description: Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three scores, and No. 25 Missouri's defense shut down star running back Jadan Baugh in a 45-17 victory Saturday afternoon over No. 8 Florida in Columbia, Mo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Austin Simmons threw for 340 yards and two touchdowns, Jamal Roberts ran for 211 yards and three scores, and No. 25 Missouri's defense shut down star running back Jadan Baugh in a 45-17 victory Saturday afternoon over No. 8 Florida in Columbia, Mo. Roberts broke two long second-half runs, one for 77 yards and later an 80-yard touchdown for the Tigers, who scored 35 straight points after the score was tied 10-10 late in the first half, scoring on six straight possessions. Mizzou coach Eli Drinkwitz improved to 2-10 against teams ranked in the Top 10 of the Associated Press poll. Simmons hooked up with Donovan Olugbode on a 47-yard touchdown pass, and with Caleb Goodie Sr. on a 31-yard score in the second quarter. Cayden Lee led the Tigers (4-1, 1-1 Southeastern Conference), with 110 receiving yards on eight catches. Simmons finished 23-of-30 passing. Baugh, a Heisman Trophy candidate after the first month of the season, gained only 13 rushing yards on 12 carries for the Gators (4-1, 2-1). He came in with 11 touchdowns to lead FBS, and had rushed for at least 100 yards in five straight games dating back to last season. No. 2 Georgia 38, Vanderbilt 14 Gunner Stockton completed 25 of 32 passes for 295 yards and three touchdowns to help lead the Bulldogs to victory over the Commodores in Athens, Ga. Stockton connected with 10 receivers, including Dwight Phillips Jr., who had five catches for 75 yards and a score. The Bulldogs (5-0, 3-0 SEC) have won all their games by at least 24 points. They outscored the Commodores 17-0 in the second half after going into halftime with a 21-14 lead. Vanderbilt (3-2, 0-2) was without freshman quarterback Jared Curtis, who was scratched before the game with an undisclosed injury. In his place, Blaze Berlowitz completed 12 of 23 passes for 190 yards and a touchdown. Junior Sherrill posted seven receptions for 107 yards and a score for the Commodores, who dropped their second straight game. No. 3 Notre Dame 37, North Carolina 26 CJ Carr threw for four touchdowns and ran for another as the Fighting Irish beat the Tar Heels in rainy conditions in Chapel Hill, N.C. Jordan Faison caught two touchdown passes as part of an eight-catch, 132-yard receiving effort for Notre Dame (5-0). Carr completed 21 of 29 passes for 234 yards. Jonaz Walton rushed for 120 yards on 23 carries. Billy Edwards Jr. threw for three touchdowns, two interceptions and 208 yards for North Carolina (2-2), which was held to 285 yards of total offense. Jordan Shipp had 109 receiving yards on seven catches. No. 4 Miami 41, Clemson 13 Mark Fletcher Jr. ran for two touchdowns and Darian Mensah passed for a TD and ran for another to lead the Hurricanes in a rout of the host Tigers. Miami (5-0, 3-0 Atlantic Coast Conference) moved into sole possession of first place in the league standings while beating Clemson (3-2, 2-1) on its home field for the first time since 2010. Fletcher finished with 77 yards on 16 carries. Mensah completed 18 of 27 passes for 227 yards. The Hurricanes' defense recorded six sacks, including five in the first half, against Clemson quarterback Tait Reynolds. He completed 29 of 44 passes for 295 yards with no touchdowns and one interception, which resulted in a 39-yard pick-six by Miami's JJ Dunnigan to close the scoring. No. 5 Ohio State 31, No. 14 Iowa 14 Jeremiah Smith set two more school records and strengthened his Heisman Trophy candidacy as the Buckeyes defeated the Hawkeyes in Iowa City. Smith, a junior, made his 36th career touchdown catch in the third quarter to surpass Chris Olave's school record and give Ohio State a 24-6 lead. On Ohio State's next drive, Smith's 10th catch of the game was his 206th for the Buckeyes to move one ahead of former record-holder Emeka Egbuka. Smith finished with 11 catches for 206 yards. Iowa finished with just 238 total yards and lost the turnover battle 2-0. No. 6 Indiana 47, Rutgers 15 Josh Hoover was 20-for-27 passing for 251 yards and four touchdowns, Turbo Richard racked up a career-high 204 yards and a score on the ground and the Hoosiers thrashed the Scarlet Knights in Piscataway, N.J. The Hoosiers (5-0, 2-0 Big Ten) extended the nation's longest winning streak to 21. Lee Beebe Jr. had a big second half to finish with 122 rushing yards and a touchdown, while Charlie Becker made eight catches for 107 yards and two TDs. Indiana became the first Big Ten team with two 100-yard rushers and two 100-yard receivers in one game since 1995. Rutgers' AJ Surace relieved Dylan Lonergan at quarterback before halftime, with Lonergan apparently injured on a QB sneak attempt. Surace was the more effective passer for the Scarlet Knights (1-4, 0-2), with 128 yards and a 53-yard touchdown to Ben Black III. No. 7 Alabama 56, No. 16 Mississippi State 23 Keelon Russell totaled four touchdowns, as the Crimson Tide rolled past the Bulldogs in an SEC clash in Starkville, Miss. Russell threw for 285 yards and three touchdowns and ran for one more. Rico Scott had 56 receiving yards and two touchdowns for Alabama (5-0, 3-0 SEC), which is 5-0 for the first time in Kalen DeBoer's three seasons. Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor completed 19 of 34 passes for 258 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions. The Bulldogs have lost 17 straight games against the Crimson Tide. Taylor went to the locker room with an undisclosed injury early in the fourth quarter, and reserve Parker Puckett finished the game under center. No. 10 BYU 17, TCU 10 Quarterback Bear Bachmeier rushed for two touchdowns and Faletau Satuala recorded a key interception as the Cougars downed the Horned Frogs in Big 12 play at Fort Worth, Texas. Bachmeier rushed for 66 yards on 15 carries and completed 11 of 24 passes for 62 yards for BYU (4-0, 2-0 Big 12), which has started 4-0 in three consecutive seasons for the first time in program history. Star running back LJ Martin carried the ball just twice for 16 yards before exiting in the first quarter with a right leg injury. The reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year was ruled out at halftime. Jaden Craig was 18-of-25 passing for 187 yards, one touchdown and one interception for TCU (2-3, 0-2). Kari Ashley had six receptions for 108 yards and one touchdown and Jeremy Payne had 100 yards from scrimmage (77 rushing, 23 receiving). No. 11 LSU 63, McNeese 14 Sam Leavitt passed for three touchdowns in limited action, Corey Barber Jr. caught two of the scoring passes, Harlem Berry and Stacy Gage each rushed for more than 100 yards as the host Tigers thrashed the FCS-level Cowboys in Baton Rouge, La. Leavitt, who has been hampered by a hamstring injury, did not run the ball and played just the first half before being relieved by Landen Clark with LSU (4-1) leading 35-0. Leavitt passed for 176 yards and an interception. Barber, a freshman who had just one reception for 15 yards before Saturday, finished with seven catches for 83 yards and his first career TDs. Berry had the first 100-yard rushing game of his two-year career, finishing with 125 yards and a score, and Gage rushed for 110 yards and two TDs on six carries. The Tigers outgained McNeese (2-4) 731-196 and finished with a 37-6 advantage in first downs. No. 12 Texas Tech 29, Colorado 7 John Curry intercepted a pass in the end zone for a touchdown, Brice Pollock had two interceptions and Malik Esquerra added another pick as the Red Raiders rallied for a victory over the Buffaloes in Boulder, Colo. All three third-quarter Colorado (2-3, 0-2 Big 12) drives ended in interceptions as the Red Raiders (5-0, 2-0) overcame a 7-3 halftime deficit. As Curry rushed off the edge with 7:10 remaining in the game, he reached up and intercepted Colorado quarterback Isaac Wilson's pass in the end zone for a 22-7 lead. Texas Tech's Will Hammond threw for 134 yards and a touchdown. J'Koby Williams rushed for 88 yards and Quinten Joyner ran in a score. Wilson was 26 of 44 for 290 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions. Joseph Williams caught 10 passes for 93 yards and a score and threw an interception on a trick play. No. 17 Tennessee 24, Auburn 14 DeSean Bishop rushed for a career-high 220 yards and three second-half touchdowns to rally the Volunteers past the Tigers in the first matchup between these SEC foes since 2020 in Knoxville, Tenn. The former walk-on from Knoxville carried 34 times while becoming the first Tennessee running back to go for 200 yards and three scores since Eric Gray in 2019. Tennessee coach Josh Heupel benched freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon late in the first half after he went 3-for-8 passing for no yards and one interception. Backup George MacIntyre completed 8 of 10 passes for 86 yards. Auburn's Byrum Brown was 22-for-33 passing for 159 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. He rushed for 107 yards on 19 attempts and scored the first touchdown for the Tigers, who built a 7-3 halftime lead. No. 18 Southern California 25, Washington 21 The Trojans scored a pair of third-quarter touchdowns less than two minutes apart, then held firm on the Huskies' final drive to survive with a win in Los Angeles. The Trojans (5-1, 2-1 Big Ten Conference) surrendered a pair of fourth-down conversions that allowed the Huskies (3-2, 0-2) to advance into the red zone with less than a minute remaining in regulation. USC's defense buckled down, however. USC's Jayden Maiava finished with one of his more statistically muted efforts, going 21-of-34 passing for 245 yards with a touchdown and an interception. King Miller led the Trojans with 81 yards rushing. Demond Williams Jr. finished 15-of-26 passing for 198 yards and one touchdown and Brian Bonner rushed for 89 yards for Washington. No. 20 Houston 27, UCF 17 Conner Weigman scored three times on the ground in the second half as the host Cougars shrugged off a ragged first 40 minutes and roared from behind to beat UCF. Weigman's third rushing touchdown, a 1-yard plunge with 10:15 to play, gave Houston (4-1, 1-1 Big 12) its first lead. On the ensuing drive, Weigman -- who finished with 239 passing yards -- connected with Trent Walker for a 43-yard catch-and-run to set the table for Jonathan Dimas' 40-yard field goal with 4:14 to play. Keyone Jenkins passed for 253 yards and a touchdown and ran for another score to lead UCF's (3-2, 1-1) attack. Josh Derry caught seven passes for 101 yards and one touchdown. No. 21 SMU 25, Boston College 16 The host Mustangs carried a three-point lead into halftime and nearly pitched a second-half shutout in a win over the Eagles. Kevin Jennings threw touchdowns to Randy Pittman Jr. and Derrick McFall after intermission, finishing 20-for-30 passing for 160 yards. SMU (4-1, 2-1 ACC) sacked Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie five times and held the Eagles (2-3, 0-2) scoreless over seven straight possessions from the first quarter until a touchdown with 2:07 left in regulation. Marques White recorded three of the five sacks. McKenzie also threw for two scores and 208 yards on a 20-of-31 passing day. He also led all ball carriers with 74 yards on 21 attempts. Evan Dickens and Danny Edgehill each caught one touchdown pass. No. 22 Boise State 37, Utah State 18 Maddux Madsen passed for two touchdowns and Dylan Riley rushed for two scores as the Broncos ran away with a victory over the Aggies in the inaugural Pac-12 contest for both teams at Boise, Idaho. Madsen completed 17 of 21 passes for 244 yards as the Broncos (4-1, 1-0 Pac-12) defeated Utah State for the 11th consecutive time and 23rd time in the past 24 meetings. Matt Wagner and Ben Ford caught touchdown passes for Boise State, which also saw Jake Ripp return an interception for a touchdown. Javen Jacobs caught a touchdown pass and rushed for 139 yards on 10 carries, including gains of 64 and 46 yards for Utah State (1-4, 0-1). Eli Wood had seven receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown. Grady Brosterhous completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards and two touchdowns. No. 24 Kentucky 35, South Carolina 34 (OT) Kenny Minchey's two-point-conversion pass to Willie Rodriguez lifted the Wildcats to an overtime win over the Gamecocks in Columbia, S.C. Minchey connected with Henry Boyer on a 6-yard touchdown to set up the successful two-point attempt and cap the largest road comeback in program history after Kentucky (4-1, 2-1 SEC) trailed 17-0 in the second quarter. Minchey had 272 passing yards and three touchdowns. LaNorris Sellers threw for 226 yards and two touchdowns while rushing 17 times for 147 yards. Matt Fuller and Jabree Coleman each had a rushing touchdown, while Mazeo Bennett Jr. had 92 receiving yards, and DJ Black and Brown each caught a touchdown pass for South Carolina (2-3, 0-3). --Field Level Media

item.title: Tarik Skubal pitches Dodgers past Braves in Game 1 of NLDS
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened the National League Division Series with a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: LOS ANGELES -- Tarik Skubal dominated over six innings, three home runs powered the offense and the Los Angeles Dodgers opened the National League Division Series with a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Saturday. Teoscar Hernandez, Kyle Tucker and Max Muncy all went deep as the Dodgers started their quest to become the first National League club to win three consecutive championships and the first major league team to do it since the New York Yankees from 1998-2000. Skubal (1-0) gave up one run on two hits with two walks and seven strikeouts in his first postseason start for Los Angeles after arriving in a trade-deadline deal from the Detroit Tigers. Sean Murphy and Ozzie Albies hit home runs for the Braves, who entered off a wild-card round victory over the Philadelphia Phillies and are trying to advance past the NLDS for the first time since winning the World Series in 2021. Left-hander Dylan Dodd opened the game with three scoreless innings for Atlanta before giving way to Victor Mederos (0-1), who gave up Hernandez's home run and recorded just one out in the fourth inning. On a blisteringly hot day, with the temperature at 100 degrees to open the game, Skubal allowed only one hit through his first five scoreless innings on the mound. Hernandez backed Skubal with a two-run home run in the fourth inning for a 2-0 advantage. "I really don't care if I strike out in big situations. I always want to be the guy to be in those moments," Hernandez said. "I worked really hard for it, and I think the bigger the moment, the more focused I get. Just trying to put together a good at-bat for the team. Obviously if I get a good pitch to hit, I just try to put a good swing on it." The Braves finally got to Skubal in the sixth when Murphy hit a home run to center to bring Atlanta to within a run. The Dodgers increased their advantage in the bottom of the sixth against AJ Smith-Shawver when Tucker slugged a two-run home run and Muncy followed two batters later with a solo shot down the line in right field for a 5-1 advantage. Tucker's contribution on offense came after a disappointing regular season when his .715 OPS was lower than all but one Dodgers player who played in at least 90 games. Tucker is in the first season of a four-year, $240 million contract. Albies got the Braves within two runs in the ninth with a two-run home run off Tanner Scott. Evan Phillips entered the game with two outs and walked Mauricio Dubon to bring the tying run to the plate. But he earned the save by retiring Austin Riley on a groundout to short. "I thought we put up some competitive at-bats. Really nice swing from Murphy right there and then and then not giving up," Riley said. "With Ozzie, the two-run homer, that was encouraging. Just ran out of time today." --Doug Padilla, Field Level Media

item.title: Panthers place WR Xavier Legette on IR
item.description: The Carolina Panthers placed wide receiver Xavier Legette on injured reserve Saturday due to a knee injury.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Carolina Panthers placed wide receiver Xavier Legette on injured reserve Saturday due to a knee injury. He is set to miss at least the next four weeks. In Week 2, the 25-year-old reeled in a 55-yard reception against the Atlanta Falcons but sustained a knee injury on the play. He sat out of the team's Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Legette was a first-round pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Across his first two seasons, he recorded 924 yards and seven touchdowns in 33 games (25 starts). The Panthers' receiving group could look thin on Sunday against the Detroit Lions. Leading receiver Jalen Coker (quadriceps) is listed as questionable. On Saturday, the team also promoted wide receiver Ja'seem Reed from the practice squad. Reed went undrafted in 2025 out of San Diego and is in line to potentially make his NFL debut. --Field Level Media

item.title: Britain scraps heavily criticised plans to curb jury trials after backlash
item.description: Britain will scrap plans to remove the historic right to trial by jury for defendants in less serious criminal cases, the government announced on Sunday, in response to sustained criticism of the proposals by many lawyers and politicians.
item.dc:creator: Sam Tobin
item.content:encoded: Britain will scrap plans to remove the historic right to trial by jury for defendants in less serious criminal cases, the government announced on Sunday, in response to sustained criticism of the proposals by many lawyers and politicians. The decision by Andy Burnham, who became prime minister in July, to drop his predecessor Keir Starmer's policy comes as hundreds of prisoners were released early to stop prisons becoming full, in just one element of a criminal justice crisis. Plans to [USN:L8N3X80VW TEXT:"curb jury trials"] for cases where a jail sentence was likely to be less than three years would be abandoned, the Ministry of Justice said, which was broadly welcomed by the Criminal Bar Association and other groups. But lawyers raised concerns over the MoJ's decision to increase sentencing powers for magistrates – who hear trials for more minor offences without a jury – and the removal of defendants' right to elect trial by jury. "I have heard the strength of feeling on the proposals for increasing the number of judge-alone trials in the Crown Court and have made the decision to change course," Justice Secretary Alex Norris said. CBA chair Andrew Thomas thanked the government for "listening to the evidence and reaching the right verdict", though he said "a severe threat to our trial by jury remains". The Bar Council's chair Kirsty Brimelow agreed, saying that giving magistrates greater powers when the backlog in magistrates' courts is increasing could be counterproductive. VICTIMS WAITING YEARS FOR JUSTICE The current backlog of [USN:L8N3T512N TEXT:"cases awaiting trial"] by jury in Crown Courts in England and Wales was nearly 81,000 at the end of June, almost double the figure in 2020, and victims, defendants and witnesses often wait years for cases to come to trial. Starmer's justice minister David Lammy last year said reducing jury trials would speed up justice, but met a furious backlash from lawyers who said it curtailed the fundamental right of defendants to be tried by a jury of their peers. Critics also argued that years of neglect and under-investment by successive governments, rather than jury trials, were the root cause of delays, while the head of England's judiciary raised "grave security concerns" for judges. The MoJ said it would maintain plans that complex fraud trials could be heard by a judge alone, which has long been mooted to avoid jurors sitting on months-long cases, though a government-commissioned review this year rejected the idea.

item.title: Trump names intelligence chief Clayton as AI czar, to head task force, WSJ reports
item.description: US President Donald Trump has appointed Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as the administration's AI czar, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing an interview with Clayton.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump has appointed Director of National Intelligence [USN:L1N4400P3 TEXT:"Jay Clayton"] as the administration's AI czar, the Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing an interview with Clayton. Clayton, who was [USN:L1N4400P3 TEXT:"appointed"] intelligence chief in August, will lead a new White House panel tasked with reporting within 120 days on the risks and opportunities posed by AI, the newspaper said. "The president asked that a group be put together," which the administration refers to as the "Super Intelligence Force," to ensure the US remains a leader in advanced AI while protecting Americans' interests, Clayton told the Journal, adding that "the risk of not being first is high." The safety of AI has become a major issue in recent weeks, with some researchers warning that people building the technology believe it could [USN:L4N45616J TEXT:"kill humans within a decade."] Several Democratic and Republican lawmakers have responded with alarm and calls for more action. Trump has appeared to take a [USN:FWN45G0T8 TEXT:"light touch"] toward AI regulation, arguing that excessive oversight could weaken competitiveness against China. He said on Tuesday that he [USN:RTV7Cd7Qt TEXT:"does not want to work"] with Chinese President Xi Jinping on governing AI technology. Clayton's panel will review AI-related risks and current government reporting mechanisms for breaches, hacks and other incidents, and recommend ways to strengthen federal-response capabilities under existing authorities, the Journal said, citing the task force's charter. This is the second time Trump has named an adviser to oversee AI-related decisions across the administration. Venture capitalist David Sacks held the AI czar role at the beginning of Trump's second term. The task force's vice chairs will be Emil Michael, Scott Kupor and Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, while members will include Vice President JD Vance, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Treasury Secretary [USN:L6N45H0WJ TEXT:"Scott Bessent"] and White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles, according to the report. External advisers will also include Sacks and former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, the Journal said.
